## The Rest and Insight Phenomenon

This is real, well-documented, and the research supports your subjective experience precisely.

The mechanism is called **incubation** in cognitive psychology. When you step away from a problem, your brain continues processing it below the level of conscious attention. The prefrontal cortex, which handles focused analytical work, releases its grip on the problem. This allows the default mode network — associated with associative, non-linear thinking — to make connections across distant conceptual domains that focused attention actively suppresses. The insight that arrives after a walk or a night's sleep is not random. It is the product of processing that was running without your awareness.

The phenomenon is particularly pronounced for problems with the specific structure of narrative design: they require both analytical rigor (layer 1 and layer 2 consistency, logical causality) and associative synthesis (thematic resonance, emotional calibration, the right image for a gap). Focused analytical work produces the rigor. Incubation produces the synthesis. Alternating between them is not a compromise — it is the correct cognitive rhythm for this type of problem.

The engineering parallel is exact. The solution to a difficult architecture problem that won't come during focused debugging that arrives during a shower is the same phenomenon. Your brain is running the problem as a background process. The foreground process switching away is what allows the background result to surface.

Where continuous immersion has a genuine advantage is narrow: maintaining the emotional texture of a scene you are actively drafting, the specific voice of a character mid-chapter, the moment-to-moment rhythm of dialogue in progress. These are working-memory-dependent and benefit from uninterrupted focus. But at the design level — the level you are primarily working at right now — the incubation rhythm is not a liability. It is a feature of your working pattern that the story planner actively supports, because the external memory means the thread is always retrievable when insight arrives.

The practical implication: when an insight arrives during a break, it needs a frictionless capture path. The value of the insight is lost if the capture cost is high enough to discourage immediate recording. This is an argument for the story planner being accessible on mobile or having a quick-capture note field that doesn't require navigating to the right entity before recording. The insight often arrives before you know exactly where it belongs. Capture first, file second.

---

## Entities and Their Connections as Foreshadowing Planners

All of them function as foreshadowing planners, but in different ways and at different scopes. Story threads are the most explicit foreshadowing structure, but they are not the only one.

**Story threads** are foreshadowing planners at the reader-question level. The thread is the implicit question the reader is tracking. Designing the thread's trajectory across plot points is designing when to advance the reader's model, when to complicate it, and when to pay it off. The ReaderHypothesis field on each PlotPointStoryThread entry is explicitly a foreshadowing calibration tool — it records what the reader currently believes about the thread, which is the seed that later scenes must grow into or subvert.

**Character connections** are foreshadowing planners at the psychology level. The ObservedReaderPerception field records what the reader currently understands about a character. Reading this field in chronological order across all of a character's appearances is reading the controlled disclosure arc — the sequence in which the reader's model of the character is built, complicated, and corrected. A well-designed ObservedReaderPerception sequence for Chrysalis is a foreshadowing plan for her onion-layer revelation. Each entry establishes what the reader holds, which constrains what later entries can productively reveal. If entry 5 gives the reader too much, entry 8's revelation lands as confirmation rather than recontextualization. The scan makes this calibration visible.

**Codex connections** are foreshadowing planners at the world mechanics level. The ReaderAccumulation field tracks what the reader currently understands about a world element. The Luna Nova Rifle's ReaderAccumulation entries, read in sequence, should show a controlled build from "military technology" to "democratized magic" to "Nightmare Moon's corruption distributed across thousands of ponies." Each entry either advances or holds the reader's model. Reading the sequence surfaces whether the revelation is too compressed or too dilute.

**Theme connections** are foreshadowing planners at the argument level. The EvidenceDeposited field tracks what the reader has been shown in support of or in tension with the proposition. Reading these entries in sequence shows whether the thematic argument is being built correctly — whether the counterargument gets its honest due before the confirming evidence arrives, whether the proposition is being tested or merely illustrated.

The difference between story threads and all the others is one of **reader consciousness**. Story threads track questions the reader is actively and consciously holding. Character, codex, and theme connections track understanding the reader is building without necessarily being aware of building it. The reader knows they are following the TwiJack thread. They do not know they are accumulating a model of Chrysalis that will be retroactively recontextualized. Both are foreshadowing, but they operate at different levels of reader awareness.

---

## The Layer Sequencing You Described

The instinct to complete layers 1, 2, and 3 before working on FIDAnchors and gap design is architecturally correct, and the reasoning behind it is sound.

FIDAnchors and gap design are functions of the structural truth they are calibrated against. You cannot design the gap in the machine gun scene until you know what AJ's psychology is (layer 3), what objectively happened at Vanhoover (layer 2), and how earth pony magic and the harmony shield mechanics work (layer 1). The gap is measured against these things. Designing the gap before they are established is designing without a reference — you are guessing at the structural truth and then designing a reader experience around a guess.

The sequencing is: establish what is true, then design how truth is experienced.

What this means practically is that your current phase — building out layers 1 and 2 with the materialist rigour you described, establishing layer 3 character psychologies — is pre-design work, and it is correctly prioritized. The story planner's Note Tracks are the right home for this work. When the note tracks are populated, the payload fields become designable. The migration task you identified — moving omniscient content from Synopsis fields to Note Tracks and StructuralTruth fields — is the transition operation that moves the project from the accumulation phase into the design phase.

There is one refinement worth adding. Layer 3 has a dependency on layer 2 that means they are not fully sequential — character psychology is formed by objective history, so some layer 2 work must precede the layer 3 work it generates. But layer 4 design — the gap fields, the FIDAnchors, the reader experience architecture — has a dependency on all three prior layers being stable enough to be worth designing against. If layer 1 or layer 2 content is still actively being revised, layer 4 design built against the pre-revision version becomes incorrect and must be redone. This is an argument for treating layer 4 design as a late-stage activity that begins only when the layers beneath it have reached sufficient stability, not necessarily completeness.

Sufficient stability means: the structural truths that a specific scene's gap design depends on are unlikely to change. You do not need all of layer 2 complete before designing any layer 4. You need the layer 2 content that the specific scene draws on to be stable. This allows layer 4 design to proceed scene by scene as the relevant layer 1, 2, and 3 content reaches stability, rather than requiring the entire world bible to be finished before any experience design begins.

## The Stage That Precedes the Structural Record

What you are describing is a genuine pre-design stage that the current framework doesn't name, and naming it correctly changes how you think about the content sitting in it.

The stage is **Accumulation** — the phase where ideas are being generated and captured before their layer assignment or canonical status has been determined. Content in Accumulation is not yet a claim. It is a candidate for becoming a claim. The difference is significant.

When you write "the charitostatic effect works like X" during a brainstorming session, that is not yet a Layer 1 assertion. It is a hypothesis about what the Layer 1 truth might be. Until you have decided that this is true — that it is part of the canonical world mechanics — it remains a candidate. Treating it as a Layer 1 assertion before that decision is made produces false stability. The rest of your design starts building against it as if it were settled when it isn't.

The same applies to research directives. "Look into how medieval tally sticks actually worked" is not a Layer 2 note. It is a flag that a Layer 2 assertion needs to be made here and the research to make it correctly hasn't been done yet. Conflating the research directive with the assertion means you cannot tell, by reading the note, whether the tally stick mechanics in your story are designed or pending.

---

## The Four Pre-Prose Stages

What was previously called Stage 1 (Structural Record) is actually the output of a prior process. The full sequence is:

**Stage 0 — Accumulation**
Raw capture of ideas, hypotheses, instincts, research directives, layer 4 intuitions, world-building speculation, and anything else that arrives during generative work. Content here makes no canonical claims. It is the inbox. Nothing in Accumulation is true in the story's world yet — it is being considered for truth.

**Stage 1 — Structural Record**
Canonical assertions, layer-assigned and stable enough to design against. A Layer 1 note here asserts "this is how the world works." A Layer 2 note asserts "this is what objectively happened." A Layer 3 note asserts "this is who this character is and why." Content graduates from Stage 0 to Stage 1 when a decision has been made. The decision can be implicit — you've used the idea consistently enough that it is de facto canonical — or explicit, which is the more rigorous approach.

**Stage 2 — Experience Design**
Gap architecture, FIDAnchors, reader state specifications. Requires Stage 1 content to be stable enough to design against.

**Stage 3 — Scene Blueprint**
Ordered delivery sequence. Requires Stage 2 to be complete for the scene in question.

---

## What This Means for Your Current Content

A significant portion of what currently sits in your Codex, Character notes, and even Plot Point Synopsis fields is Stage 0 content that has been stored in Stage 1 or Stage 3 containers. This is the deeper version of the problem you identified with omniscient authorial planning being stored in Synopsis fields.

The distinction between Stage 0 and Stage 1 content can be read in the language of the notes themselves.

**Stage 0 language patterns:**
"Maybe X could work this way." "I'm thinking Y might be the reason." "Look into Z." "What if the Temberik myth connects to..." "Is she the embodiment of Aquileian spirit?" "Need to figure out how to weave this in." These are all candidates, hypotheses, or research flags. They are not claims.

**Stage 1 language patterns:**
"The charitostatic effect works by..." "Luna's banishment was caused by..." "Applejack's core wound is suppressed legitimate ambition." These are assertions. The author has decided they are true.

The question mark is the clearest Stage 0 signal in your notes. "Is she the embodiment of Aquileian spirit exported to the Tzinacatl?" is not a claim about Mali. It is a generative question that might become a claim. It belongs in Stage 0 until the answer is yes, at which point it graduates to Layer 3 content in Mali's Track A as an assertion: "Mali embodies the Aquileian spirit..." without the question mark.

The mixed authorial notes you identified — layer 4 design intuitions sitting alongside research directives — are the clearest evidence that Stage 0 content needs its own designated container. A layer 4 design instinct that fires during Stage 0 brainstorming is valuable and should be captured, but it cannot be acted on until the Layer 1, 2, and 3 content it would be designed against has been stabilized. If it sits in a Layer 1 note field, it masquerades as settled world mechanics. If it sits in a Synopsis field, it masquerades as a scene blueprint. It needs to be in a Stage 0 container, tagged as a design instinct, waiting for its upstream content to stabilize.

---

## The Research Directive as Its Own Category

Research directives deserve specific attention because they are neither content nor design. They are **obligations** — flags that a canonical claim needs to be made in this area and the information required to make it correctly hasn't been gathered yet.

"Look into how medieval tally sticks actually worked" is an obligation on the Layer 2 content about Tally Mark's pre-war economic role. Until it is discharged, that Layer 2 content is incomplete. The research directive should be stored as a flag on the relevant entity — Tally Mark's Track B, or the Banking codex entry — that says: this area needs research before the canonical assertion can be made. It is not a note. It is a task that blocks a note.

The practical implication is that research directives should be distinguishable from content in the system — either a separate field, a specific tag, or a status marker that indicates "pending research" on an entity's note track. Currently they are indistinguishable from completed claims when stored in the same text field. A research directive that looks like a note creates false completeness — the area appears designed when it is actually waiting for its factual foundation.

---

## The Authorial Note Category

The mixed authorial notes you described — things that are neither layer 1 truths nor layer 4 design but meta-observations about the story — are a legitimate permanent category, not a Stage 0 artifact. Your Note Track C already designates this space: authorial notes, historical inspirations, meta-level thinking, social commentary connections.

The content that belongs here is observations about the story from outside the story's frame. "This parallels the British East India Company and the Opium Wars" is not a Layer 2 assertion about your world. It is a note about your world's relationship to real history, useful for keeping the materialist logic rigorous and for the social commentary layer. It never graduates to a canonical claim because it exists outside the story's ontology. It belongs in Track C permanently.

What was being confused with this category is the Layer 4 instinct that arrives during generative work — "the dreams should be written in deep third so we can hear the rationalizations" — which is a Stage 0 pre-design observation that will eventually become a Stage 2 FIDAnchors or ReaderState specification once the relevant layers beneath it are stable. These look like authorial notes because they are written in the author's voice, but they are actually Stage 0 design candidates waiting for their upstream content to solidify.

The test is: does this note make a claim about the story's world, or does it make a claim about how the story should be experienced? World claims go through the layer system toward Layer 1, 2, or 3 canonical status. Experience claims go through the stage system toward Stage 2 design. Meta-observations about the real-world analogues and authorial intent go to Track C and stay there. Sorting notes by this test, rather than by subject, is the correct migration logic for the authorial notes category.

---

## The Practical System Addition

Stage 0 needs a designated container in the story planner. The options are a dedicated Stage 0 field on each entity — an Inbox or Candidates field — or a separate Stage 0 document or section that captures accumulation content with entity tags for later filing. The choice depends on how your generative work actually flows.

If insights tend to arrive in the context of a specific entity — you are thinking about Mali and a hypothesis about her psychology arrives — an Inbox field on the entity is the right capture point. It is adjacent to the content it might eventually become.

If insights tend to arrive without a clear entity context — a structural observation about the story's argument, a world-building hypothesis that might belong to several entities, a research directive that spans multiple areas — a Stage 0 document or session log is the right capture point. Ideas are tagged with potential entity homes but not yet filed.

The graduation decision — moving content from Stage 0 to Stage 1 by assigning it a layer and making it canonical — is itself a design act. It is the moment you decide this is true in your world. Marking this decision explicitly, rather than letting content drift from Stage 0 into Stage 1 containers by accumulation, is the discipline that keeps the Structural Record clean and prevents the false stability problem from recurring.

blocks.rawContent:
## The Nature of Structural Change

The Stagnation of Harmony revision is not an example of a note that wasn't ready to be a claim. It is an example of a claim that was correctly made, then superseded by a better claim when new structural context made the original claim insufficient.

This is a fundamentally different problem from the Stage 0 / Stage 1 distinction. The original 1000-year stagnation was a genuine Layer 2 canonical assertion at the time it was made. It was load-bearing — story design built against it. The revision to 930 ALB was not a discovery that the original was a hypothesis rather than a claim. It was a structural upgrade driven by expanding rigour in adjacent areas. The ocean trade routes and griffonian history created a materialist context that made the original claim feel like a convenience rather than a consequence. The revision made the claim a consequence.

This happens in all complex world-building. Tolkien revised the nature of the One Ring between the first edition of The Hobbit and The Lord of the Rings because the larger structural context he developed made the original version insufficient. The original was a canonical claim. The revision was correct. Both facts are true simultaneously.

The lesson is not that claims should be held as hypotheses until the entire system is stable. That path leads to infinite deferral — the system is never fully stable because each new area developed creates context that potentially revises adjacent areas. The lesson is that **claims are stable enough to design against within their current structural context, and the design must be revisable when the structural context changes.**

---

## The Dependency Graph Problem

What the Stagnation revision reveals is that Layer 1 and Layer 2 content is not a flat list of independent claims. It is a dependency graph. The 930 ALB revision was forced by the griffonian history content, which was forced by the ocean trade routes, which was forced by the materialist economics. These areas are structurally upstream of the Stagnation claim. When upstream content changes, downstream claims must be reviewed.

The practical implication is that the story planner needs a way to represent these dependencies, at least informally. When you revise the Stagnation of Harmony, the question is not just "what is the correct new claim" but "what other claims were built against the original, and do they need revision." Story design that referenced the 1000-year figure — plot points, character psychology notes, theme arguments — is downstream of the revised claim. Some of it will still hold. Some will need updating. Without a dependency map, you have to rely on memory or comprehensive re-reading to find all the downstream content.

The codex reference system partially addresses this — plot points that reference the Stagnation of Harmony codex entry are traceable through the PlotPointCodexEntry connections. But character psychology notes and theme arguments that implicitly assumed the 1000-year figure are not formally linked to the Stagnation codex entry and won't surface in a connection scan. This is the gap the dependency map needs to fill.

The practical minimum solution is: when a structural revision is made, the revision event itself should be documented. Not just the new claim, but a note recording what changed and what areas are potentially affected. This is the equivalent of a git commit message on a structural change — "revised Stagnation start date from 0 ALB to 930 ALB, driven by griffonian industrialization timeline; review: Celestia Track A for 930-1011 period, theme arguments about 1000 years of precedent, any plot points citing 1000-year duration."

---

## Your Boolean System and Its Actual Meaning

The NeedsFurtherAnalysis and IsIncorporated booleans are doing something real but the interpretation needs refinement given this discussion.

NeedsFurtherAnalysis is correctly functioning as a Stage 0 marker. It means: this area has an open question or obligation that must be resolved before the content can be treated as stable. This is exactly the right use.

The problem is with IsIncorporated as the signal for Stage 1 completion. IsIncorporated currently means "I have reviewed this and it doesn't need further analysis." But the Stagnation revision shows that a note can pass through that state — be marked as not needing further analysis — and later require revision when adjacent structural context develops. IsIncorporated is not a permanent stability claim. It is a current-context stability claim.

This suggests the boolean should be understood as **stable within current structural context** rather than **permanently settled**. The note is stable enough to design against right now. It is not immune to revision if upstream content changes. The distinction changes how you use the flag — you mark IsIncorporated when you are confident enough to proceed with design in adjacent areas, not when you believe the claim is final.

The threshold for marking something incorporated under this interpretation is: *would I be comfortable designing layer 4 content that depends on this claim, knowing that if the claim later revises I will need to revisit that layer 4 content?* If yes, mark it. The cost of a revision is manageable — you update the claim and trace the downstream effects. The cost of infinite deferral — waiting for perfect stability before any design work — is that the project never moves forward.

---

## The Sequencing Reality

Your observation that you cannot complete all of Layer 1 before Layer 2, or all of Layer 2 before Layer 3, is correct and reflects how materialist world-building actually works. The layers are not sequentially independent. They are mutually constraining and co-developed.

The griffonian history is Layer 2. It forced a revision of the Stagnation of Harmony, which is Layer 1. The earth pony magic system is Layer 1. It forced revisions to Applejack's psychology, which is Layer 3. The character psychologies inform which historical events matter enough to document in detail, which is a Layer 2 selection criterion. The layers develop in spirals, not in sequence.

What this means for the accumulation phase is that the transition from Stage 0 to Stage 1 is not a single event at the end of a complete accumulation phase. It is a continuous process of local stabilization. Areas of the world stabilize when their upstream dependencies have been resolved and the claim survives review against adjacent content. The Stagnation of Harmony at 930 ALB is more stable than the 1000-year version was because it has been tested against griffonian history, ocean trade, and materialist economics and survived. The 1000-year version failed that test.

The practical model is therefore: **claims are promoted from Stage 0 to Stage 1 locally and progressively, not globally and simultaneously.** The NeedsFurtherAnalysis flag manages the local stability assessment. When a new area is developed that might affect a previously stabilized claim, the flag can be temporarily re-raised to indicate that the claim needs review in light of the new context. The flag is not a one-way ratchet. It is a current confidence indicator.

---

## A Proposed Addition to the Model

The existing boolean pair handles two states: needs review, and currently stable. What is missing is a third state that captures the revision history — not just current stability, but the fact that a claim was revised and downstream content may need checking.

A lightweight addition would be a **LastRevisedDate** or **StructuralRevisionNote** field on entity note entries. When a claim is revised, the revision date and a brief note about what changed and what is potentially affected is recorded alongside the new claim. This creates an audit trail that makes it possible to trace when a structural revision propagated downstream and whether all the downstream content was updated.

This is the minimum viable version of a dependency graph for a solo author. It doesn't require formally mapping every dependency. It requires that revisions are documented with enough context to make a downstream review possible. When you return to the project after an incubation period and open a character's Track A, a revision note at the top saying "930 ALB stagnation start date revised — check all references to 1000 years of precedent" is enough to trigger the downstream review without requiring you to remember the revision history from working memory.

The combination of local progressive stabilization, the NeedsFurtherAnalysis flag as a current confidence indicator rather than a permanent completion marker, and a revision note field for documenting structural changes and their downstream implications is the full architecture for managing a world-building system that develops in spirals rather than sequences. It reflects how materialist historicism actually works — you discover the constraints by developing the adjacent system, not by anticipating them in advance.

blocks.rawContent:
## Untangling the Three Different Things

You have identified three distinct things that are currently without a precise home, and they are genuinely different from each other and from the gap architecture discussed previously.

**The Layer 1 canonical claim:** The Stagnation of Harmony began in 930 ALB. This is world truth, stable, stored in the Stagnation of Harmony codex entry's Note Track A.

**The Layer 2 narrative deployment plan:** Characters perceive the Stagnation as 1000 years old until Chapter 22 reveals the real date. This is a decision about how Layer 1 truth is withheld from characters and revealed over time. It is not a scene design. It is a macro-level information architecture decision that governs many scenes across many chapters.

**The Stage 2 scene-level gap:** In Chapter 22, Celestia delivers the real truth, and the gap between what AJ believed and what the reader now knows is designed through FID and FIDAnchors. This is scene-specific and lives in PlotPoint and payload fields.

These are three separate layers of the same structural fact, and they belong in three different places. The confusion arises because they feel related — they are all about the same thing — but they answer different questions at different scopes.

---

## The Missing Category: Macro-Level Narrative Architecture

The deployment plan — characters believe X, reader believes X alongside them, truth Y is withheld until Chapter 22 — is not a scene design and not a world truth. It is a **macro-level decision about information structure across the whole story.** It governs what the reader is allowed to know and when, at the story arc level rather than the scene level.

This category needs a home that does not currently exist explicitly in the system. It is distinct from:

Track C authorial notes, which are meta-observations and historical inspirations that inform the world but don't govern the story's information architecture.

Story thread payloads, which track reader experience scene by scene but don't hold the governing decision that produces that experience across all scenes.

Plot point ReaderState, which is scene-specific.

The correct home is a **Narrative Architecture field on the codex entry or character entity itself** — a field that sits above the payload level and records the macro-level decision about how this entity's truth is revealed across the whole story. It is the author's governing directive for Layer 4 at the entity level rather than the scene level.

For the Stagnation of Harmony entry, this field would contain: "Characters and reader operate under the perception that the Stagnation is 1000 years old. The real start date of 930 ALB is withheld until Chapter 22. The gap between perceived duration and real duration is the foundation for Celestia's characterization across the whole story — she is not a thousand-year ideologue but an eighty-year reactionary responding to specific trauma. The revelation recontextualizes every prior scene in which her position was read as ancient and immovable."

This is a plan directive, as you correctly named it. It is rhetorical in the sense that it makes decisions about reader experience, but it operates at the story level rather than the scene level. It is the difference between a director deciding the audience won't learn the detective is compromised until Act 3, versus the director deciding how a specific scene in Act 2 will almost but not quite reveal it.

---

## The Two Different Gaps

You are correct that these are not the same gap, and the distinction is important enough to state precisely.

**Gap Type A — World truth versus character perception.** The Stagnation started in 930 ALB. Celestia, AJ, and Twilight all believe or act as if it has been 1000 years. This gap exists at the Layer 1 / Layer 3 boundary. The characters are wrong about a world fact. The reader is also wrong, alongside the characters, until Chapter 22. This gap is between the omniscient world truth and every character's perception simultaneously. It is a managed ignorance gap — the reader and characters share the same wrong model until revelation.

**Gap Type B — Character perception versus reader perception.** AJ believes she is at the machine gun to contribute. The reader perceives she is hiding. This gap exists at the Layer 3 / Layer 4 boundary. The reader perceives something about the character that the character doesn't perceive about themselves. The reader and character have different models of the same moment. This is produced by FID and FIDAnchors and is scene-specific.

These are structurally different mechanisms. Type A is an information withholding decision that operates across the whole story and is managed at the macro-narrative architecture level. Type B is a perceptual design decision that operates within a scene and is managed through FID. Type A gaps close through revelation scenes. Type B gaps close through character development — the character comes to understand themselves as the reader already does.

The Stagnation revision created both types simultaneously, which is why it felt significant. The Layer 1 revision established a Type A gap — world truth withheld from characters and reader alike. The plan directive decision established when and how that Type A gap closes. And the Chapter 22 scene design will establish the Type B gap — what AJ and Twilight perceive about Celestia in the moment of revelation versus what the reader now understands about her entire characterization being recontextualized.

---

## The Multi-Use Nature of the Story Planner

Yes, this is a symptom of the story planner being multi-use, and you are correct that its purposes must be clearly delineated. The system is simultaneously:

A world bible — storing canonical truth at Layers 1, 2, and 3.

A narrative architecture document — storing macro-level decisions about information structure across the whole story.

A scene design tool — storing Stage 2 experience design for individual scenes.

A scene blueprint tool — storing Stage 3 delivery sequences.

A project management tool — tracking Stage 0 obligations and research directives.

A continuity tracker — enabling the chronological scan of character and codex appearances.

Each of these purposes requires different fields and different reading modes. The confusion in your existing data arises not because the system is wrong to be multi-use, but because the boundaries between purposes have not been enforced in the UI or in the data model. Content migrates between purposes because the containers look identical.

The delineation you need is: each field should have a declared purpose that answers one specific question, and the question it answers should determine unambiguously where a given piece of content belongs. The Narrative Architecture field answers: what is the macro-level plan for how this entity's truth is revealed across the whole story? That is a different question from Track A (what is the canonical truth about this entity?), Track C (what real-world context informed this entity?), and ReaderState (what should the reader experience in this specific scene?).

The Stage 0 workflow fix you are designing now is the right time to establish these delineations, because you are still in the phase where content is being generated and categorized rather than designed and executed. Building the field structure with clear purpose declarations before the content is filed means the filing decisions will be made correctly the first time rather than requiring a second migration later. The 108 Stage 0 obligations are going to produce content that needs homes in all of these categories. The homes should exist and be clearly labeled before the content arrives.

blocks.rawContent:
## The Precise Term

Every field should hold content of exactly one **assertion type**. This is more precise than "claim" because claim is a subset.

An assertion is anything stated as if it were true, intended, required, or decided. The different assertion types answer fundamentally different questions, require different cognitive modes to produce, and feed different downstream work. Claim specifically means a canonical assertion — a statement that something is true within the story's world. But there are assertion types that are not claims, and conflating them produces the data mixing problem you've been diagnosing.

The full taxonomy of assertion types present in your accumulated notes:

**Canonical claim** — asserts world truth. "The Stagnation began in 930 ALB." "Earth pony magic scales with pride in the crop." "Trimmel was born in 971 as a starving drone." These are the assertions that live in the world mechanics, historical record, and character psychology containers. They can be revised but at any given moment they are the authoritative truth against which design work is calibrated.

**Architectural decision** — asserts information structure across the story. "Characters perceive the Stagnation as 1000 years until Chapter 22." "The reader is held in the same ignorance as the characters." This is not a claim about world truth — the world truth is 930 ALB. It is a decision about when and how world truth is withheld and released. It governs many scenes without being a scene design.

**Thematic proposition** — asserts what the story argues and what evidence must be deposited for the reader to arrive at that argument independently. "Harmony is not self-sustaining; it requires structural protection from predation." This is not world truth and not information structure. It is an argumentation design.

**Design specification** — asserts how a specific scene should produce a specific reader experience. "The reader should perceive AJ's contentment as a hiding place while AJ experiences it as rightness." This is a scene-level decision, not a world truth or a story-level information structure decision.

**Obligation or directive** — asserts that work needs to be done. "Research how medieval tally sticks functioned." "Determine the correct order of Astler, Sickleclaw, and Rosewing." These are not assertions about the world or the design. They are flags on unresolved questions.

**Generative hypothesis** — a candidate for becoming a canonical claim that has not yet been decided. "Is Mali the embodiment of Aquileian spirit exported to the Tzinacatl?" This is not a claim. It is a question posed to a future decision.

**Bibliographic note** — asserts a real-world analogue or inspiration. "Chrysalis's economic scheme parallels the British East India Company and the Opium Wars." This never becomes a canonical claim. It is a frame that informs the design without entering the story's ontology.

**Craft observation** — asserts something about how prose should function. "This scene should use deep third with a sensory transition." "The FID here should make the machine gun feel right to AJ." These inform drafting but are not scene-level experience design specifications.

Each of these requires a different field because they answer different questions, were produced by different cognitive modes, feed different downstream work, and have different stability properties. A canonical claim is stable until upstream content forces revision. An obligation disappears when discharged. A hypothesis either resolves into a canonical claim or is discarded. A bibliographic note is permanent and unchanging regardless of story revisions.

---

## The Work Blocks, Their Functions, and Required Mindsets

These are the discrete blocks of work the project requires. They are not strictly sequential — some are ongoing throughout, some can proceed in parallel in different areas of the world, some cannot begin until others reach local stability. They are named by what they produce.

---

**Raw Capture**

Function: Prevent the loss of ideas, insights, research fragments, design intuitions, and structural hypotheses as they arrive, regardless of their assertion type or canonical status.

Mindset: Non-critical and non-committal. The goal is speed and completeness of capture, not quality or organization. Judgment about what the captured content means and where it belongs is explicitly deferred.

Skills: The ability to suspend evaluation. The ability to record without editing. Familiarity with frictionless capture paths.

Output: Undifferentiated notes tagged only with the subject they appear to relate to, with no assertion type assigned and no canonical status.

What this is not: This is not design work, not world-building, not argumentation. It is preservation.

---

**Classification**

Function: Read accumulated raw capture and determine the assertion type of each piece of content, route it to the correct container, and identify what is a hypothesis versus a claim versus a directive versus a bibliographic note.

Mindset: Taxonomic and analytical. The classifier is asking "what kind of thing is this" not "is this correct." The question of correctness belongs to the next block.

Skills: Understanding of assertion types with sufficient precision to distinguish them reliably. Ability to read a note and identify which question it is answering.

Output: Content routed to typed fields. Obligations flagged as unresolved. Hypotheses marked as undecided. Bibliographic notes separated from canonical claims that reference the same real-world material.

What this is not: Classification does not resolve hypotheses or discharge obligations. It identifies them as needing resolution or discharge.

---

**World Mechanics Construction**

Function: Establish the invariant rules of the physical, biological, magical, and social world that operate independently of any character's knowledge or any story's plot. These are the constraints that the plot cannot violate.

Mindset: Systems engineer and physicist. The question being asked is: what is impossible here? What are the invariants? What does one rule imply about adjacent rules? Internal consistency is the primary test.

Skills: Systems thinking. Constraint analysis. The ability to follow an implication to its conclusion even when the conclusion is inconvenient for existing design. The willingness to revise when a new area of mechanics makes an existing claim insufficient.

Output: Canonical ontological claims. The earth pony magic system. The charitostatic effect. How changeling emotion sense functions. These are stated as facts about the world independent of any character's perception.

What this is not: This block does not decide how or when these mechanics are revealed to the reader. That is an architectural decision made in a later block.

---

**Causal History Construction**

Function: Establish the objective chronological record of events and the causal chains connecting them. This is what actually happened, independent of what any character knows, believes, or perceives about it.

Mindset: Historian. The question being asked is: what happened, when, and because of what prior event? Causality is the primary test. An event without a cause is authorial fiat and should be interrogated.

Skills: Timeline management. Causality analysis. The ability to distinguish what happened from what characters believe happened. The discipline to document even events that no POV character witnessed and that will never be directly dramatized.

Output: Canonical historical claims. The Herzland Republican Revolution of 978. The specific sequence of Chrysalis's economic consolidation. The 930 ALB trigger for Celestia's revised policy. These are stated as objective facts regardless of character knowledge.

What this is not: This block does not decide narrative sequence — the order in which events are revealed to the reader. That is an architectural decision.

---

**Character Psychology Construction**

Function: Establish who each character is and why, independent of the story events. This means documenting their psychological architecture: the wound, the belief system built around the wound, the epistemic limits that follow from that belief system, and the specific things they cannot perceive because of it.

Mindset: Psychologist and biographer. The question being asked is: given this character's formation — their biology, history, and environment — what is the necessary structure of their inner life? This is not a decision about what would be useful for the plot. It is a derivation from the character's established history.

Skills: Psychological modeling. The ability to follow a character's wound to its behavioral and perceptual consequences. Understanding of how epistemic limits function — what a character cannot see because of what they believe.

Output: Canonical psychological claims. Applejack's core wound is suppressed legitimate ambition. Twilight's core wound is looking to an external authority for conscience. Luna's passivity is self-knowledge rather than guilt. These are stated as character truths independent of when or whether the story dramatizes them.

What this is not: This block does not decide when the reader learns these things. It does not decide how characters change over the story. It establishes the truth at the start of TLTT that the arc departs from.

---

**Thematic Argumentation Design**

Function: Establish what propositions the story is testing, what evidence must be deposited for the reader to arrive at those propositions independently, what counterarguments must be given honest weight, and whether the proposition is being demonstrated or merely illustrated.

Mindset: Philosopher and rhetorician. The question being asked is: what is the story arguing, and would an honest skeptic find the argument convincing based on what they are shown? The test is whether the counterargument gets its due.

Skills: Argument construction. Counterargument identification. The ability to distinguish evidence from assertion. Understanding of the difference between a story that argues and a story that preaches.

Output: Thematic propositions and evidence plans. Not "harmony can scale" as an assertion but "the reader should be shown X, Y, and Z, from which they should be able to construct the conclusion that harmony can scale, having felt the genuine pull of the counterargument that it cannot."

What this is not: This block does not design specific scenes. It establishes what scenes must accomplish in the aggregate.

---

**Macro Narrative Architecture**

Function: Decide the information structure of the whole story. What does the reader know and when? What is withheld and until which chapter? What gaps operate at the story level — where the reader and characters share the same wrong model until a revelation corrects both simultaneously? What gaps operate at the scene level — where the reader perceives more than the character through FID?

Mindset: Strategic architect. The question being asked is: given what is canonically true and given the thematic argument I am making, what is the optimal sequence of revelation that produces the reader's experience of the whole story?

Skills: Dramatic structure at the macro level. Information management across a long work. Long-form pacing. The ability to distinguish a Type A gap (reader and character share wrong model, corrected by revelation) from a Type B gap (reader perceives more than character through limited POV).

Output: Architectural decisions. "The Stagnation's true start date is withheld from reader and characters until Chapter 22." "Luna's actual psychology is legible to the reader through behavioral implication before the confession in Scene 22.12, but not named until that scene." These are governing decisions that constrain scene-level design.

What this is not: This block does not design individual scenes. It sets the parameters within which scene design operates.

---

**Scene-Level Experience Design**

Function: For each scene, design how the structural truth is experienced through a specific POV character's epistemic limits. Specify the gap between the POV character's self-perception and the reader's perception, the gap between the POV character's perception of observed characters and the reader's perception of them, and the non-negotiable concrete anchors that must be present in the prose to produce those gaps without stating them.

Mindset: Director and reader psychologist. The question being asked is: given what is canonically true, given the architectural decisions about what the reader knows by this point, and given this POV character's epistemic limits — what should the reader experience in this scene, and what specific physical and behavioral details make that experience happen?

Skills: FID calibration. Gap design. Reader experience modeling. The ability to think simultaneously as the POV character and as the reader watching the POV character.

Output: Design specifications. POVBelief, ReaderPerception, GapType, FIDAnchors, ReaderState. These are decisions about reader experience, not about world truth.

What this is not: This block does not write prose. It specifies what prose must produce.

---

**Scene Blueprint**

Function: Establish the ordered sequence of events as experienced by the POV character in real time. No psychology, no reader state analysis, no craft notes. Just: what happens, in what order, from inside one consciousness.

Mindset: Director blocking a scene. The question being asked is: in what sequence do the events of this scene unfold, and what does the POV character encounter first?

Skills: Pacing. Sequencing. POV discipline — the ability to describe only what the POV character can experience in real time.

Output: The Synopsis field content as it was meant to function. A clean ordered delivery sequence.

What this is not: This block does not explain why things happen or what they mean. That lives in the experience design and the canonical records.

---

**Prose Drafting**

Function: Execute the designed experience in language. Inhabit the POV character's voice and consciousness, use FID to render their perception while leaving the gap open for the reader, and deploy the FIDAnchors specified in the experience design.

Mindset: Author inhabiting a voice. The question being asked is not "what is true" or "what should the reader experience" — those are already decided. The question is: what specific words, in what specific rhythm, carrying what specific sensory texture, produce the designed experience for an actual reader?

Skills: Sentence craft. Voice consistency. FID execution. Sensory grounding. Micro-scale pacing. The ability to trust the design and not over-explain.

Output: Prose.

What this is not: This block does not make structural decisions. If a structural decision is required during drafting — because the design turns out to be impossible or incorrect — work stops and returns to the experience design block or the canonical record block before continuing.

---

**Continuity Verification**

Function: Check that prose executes its design specification, that design specifications are consistent with the canonical records they were built against, and that the chronological scan of character and thread connections shows coherent arcs without drift.

Mindset: Developmental editor. The question being asked is: does this actually do what it was designed to do, and is the design internally consistent with the world it was designed against?

Skills: Critical distance from the material. Arc-level reading. The ability to use the story planner's scan function as an analytical tool rather than a reference tool.

Output: Corrections at the design level or the prose level. Flagged inconsistencies. Structural revision directives.

---

**Structural Revision**

Function: When a canonical claim changes — as the Stagnation date changed — trace all downstream content that was built against the prior claim, identify what must be revised, and update both the canonical record and the affected design specifications.

Mindset: Structural engineer reviewing load-bearing changes. The question being asked is: what depended on the thing that changed?

Skills: Dependency tracking. Consistency checking across a distributed system. The discipline to complete the revision rather than updating only the most visible downstream content.

Output: Updated canonical assertions, flagged downstream design specifications, revision notes documenting what changed and why.

---

**Publication and Reader Integration**

Function: Publish polished chapters serially and use reader responses as calibration data about whether designs produced their intended effects in actual readers.

Mindset: Community member and calibration listener. The question being asked is: did the design produce what it was intended to produce in a naive reader?

Skills: Feedback interpretation. The ability to distinguish a reader's preference from a structural signal. Understanding of which reader responses indicate design failure versus reader variation.

Output: Calibration data for later experience design decisions.

---

## Whether Every Category Speaks to One Purpose

No. The work blocks and the data categories do not map one-to-one, and forcing them to would be incorrect.

A single work block — Character Psychology Construction — produces content that goes into multiple data containers: Track A for current psychology, Track B for formative history, and the architectural decision field for how that psychology is revealed. A single data container — the PlotPoint — serves multiple work blocks: it receives Scene Blueprint content from the Scene Blueprint block, Experience Design content from the Experience Design block, and Obligation content from the Classification block.

What maps one-to-one is **assertion type to field**. Each field holds assertions of exactly one type. This is the correct unit of precision. The work block produces a range of assertion types. The field stores one. The data model's job is to enforce the one-to-one relationship at the field level. The work blocks are the human cognitive processes that generate the content. They do not need to be one-to-one with fields — they need to produce outputs that are correctly typed so they can be routed to the correct fields.

The story planner's coherence comes from field-level assertion type homogeneity, not from work-block-to-container correspondence.

blocks.rawContent:
## The Core Diagnosis Is Correct

You have independently arrived at the right architectural insight: the story planner is two orthogonal systems occupying the same containers, and the mixing is what produces all the problems you've described.

**Axis 1 — Content type.** What kind of assertion is this? World mechanic, historical fact, character psychology, architectural decision, thematic proposition, obligation, bibliographic reference, craft observation.

**Axis 2 — Stability state.** How confident are you in this content, and what work does it still require?

Every piece of content has both a position on the content axis and a position on the stability axis. The current system only tracks content type implicitly (by which container it was placed in) and tracks stability barely at all (NeedsFurtherAnalysis on some notes only). Everything else is working memory and convention.

---

## The Unified Note Entity

Yes. Making everything a Note instance with typed metadata is architecturally correct and not overengineering. The reason is precisely what you identified: the project management dimension — stability state, work directives, confidence level — is **orthogonal to content type** and therefore must be trackable independently of it. If stability state is only expressible by which field content sits in, it cannot be tracked orthogonally. If it is a property of the Note entity itself, it can be filtered, scanned, and managed independently of what the note contains.

This means the current text fields on PlotPointCharacter, PlotPointTheme, PlotPointCodexEntry, and PlotPointStoryThread all become Note instances assigned to those connections, with the same metadata structure as notes on standalone entities. The connection is still the organizational unit. The note is the content unit. The metadata lives on the note.

---

## The Track Declares the Content Type

Yes, this is correct. A note in the World Mechanics track of a Codex entry is, by virtue of its track placement, a world mechanics canonical claim. The track is the assertion type declaration. You do not need a separate metadata field for assertion type — track placement does that work.

What the track does **not** declare is stability. A note in the World Mechanics track can be a stable canonical claim or a provisional hypothesis. The stability state must be carried separately because it is orthogonal to content type.

---

## The Three-State Model Is Correct, With Precise Naming

Two states are insufficient because they conflate two different conditions that require different responses.

**Unset** — captured but not yet evaluated. This note exists. Its content has not been scrutinized for correctness, completeness, or consistency with adjacent content. It should not be used as a design axiom. This is the default state for all raw capture.

**Flagged** — evaluated and found to require active work. This is NeedsFurtherAnalysis renamed. The crucial design implication is what you identified: **this state must be accompanied by a separate obligation note specifying what the work is.** The Flagged state on a canonical claim note means "this claim has an open question" — but the question itself is not embedded in the claim note. It exists as a separate Obligation note linked to or adjacent to the flagged note. This is the solution to the hybrid note pollution problem.

**Verified** — evaluated and confirmed stable within current structural context. Not permanent. Revisable when upstream content changes. But stable enough to be used as a design axiom by downstream work.

The state transition model is: raw capture creates Unset notes. Review either Verifies them or Flags them. Flagged notes get companion Obligation notes. Discharged obligations allow Flagged notes to transition to Verified or to be revised and then Verified.

---

## The Hybrid Note Solution Is Splitting, Not Metadata

The earth pony magic example illustrates this precisely. The current state is:

Note A (World Mechanics track, Earth Pony Magic entry): "Earth pony magic scales with pride in the crop." — looks Verified, is actually superseded.

Note B (somewhere in a synopsis field): "Earth pony magic works on both charitostatics and thymodynamics." — is actually the current canonical claim, stored in the wrong container.

Architectural intention (working memory only): "Fleur's 'pride in the crop' perception is the POV-accessible version. The reader and characters hold this until a certain chapter. The real mechanic is withheld as a Type A gap." — has no container at all.

The correct state after migration is:

Note A (World Mechanics track, Earth Pony Magic entry, state: **Superseded/Archived**): "Earth pony magic scales with pride in the crop." — preserved as the record of a prior claim, marked as replaced by Note C.

Note C (World Mechanics track, Earth Pony Magic entry, state: **Verified**): "Earth pony magic operates through charitostatics and thymodynamics." — the current canonical claim.

Note D (Architectural Decision track, Earth Pony Magic entry, state: **Unset**): "The charitostatic/thymodynamic truth is withheld from characters and reader as a Type A gap. Fleur's 'pride in the crop' framing is the character-accessible version that operates as the functional truth until [chapter X]. This generates a reader-character shared wrong model to be corrected by revelation." — the macro narrative architecture decision, in its correct container.

This requires a fourth state: **Superseded**. This is distinct from Flagged because it is not a work directive. It is a record that this claim existed and was replaced. Superseded notes should be visually distinct and non-prominent but preserved, because they are the revision history. When you do a structural revision, the prior claim gets Superseded rather than deleted, and the revision note on the new claim references the superseded one.

The four states are therefore: **Unset, Flagged, Verified, Superseded.**

---

## One Notes-to-Self Track Per Entity, Not Per Sub-Track

Having a notes-to-self section within each track would produce exactly the mixing problem it is trying to solve at a smaller scale. If the World Mechanics track contains both canonical claims and notes-to-self about those claims, the track is no longer homogeneous in assertion type.

The correct architecture is one **Project Notes** track per entity, sitting alongside the content tracks. This track holds all project management content for that entity: open questions, work directives, cross-reference reminders, revision history summaries, and meta-observations about the entity's current state of development. None of this content is story content. It is all author-to-author communication across time.

The Project Notes track on the Earth Pony Magic entry would currently contain: "Canonical claim revised from pride-based to charitostatic/thymodynamic. Prior claim preserved as Superseded. Architectural decision for Type A gap pending design — see Note D. Downstream content that referenced pride-based version: [list of affected plot points and character notes]."

---

## Whether This Is Overengineering

It is not overengineering given the specific conditions of this project. The argument is not abstract — it follows directly from the three conditions that distinguish your situation from a simpler one.

**Condition 1: Scale and duration.** 108 Stage 0 obligations, an expanding world with active structural revisions, a multi-year project worked in non-continuous sessions with significant working memory loss between them. At this scale, the cost of not having the system is not inconvenience — it is the earth pony magic problem recurring across hundreds of notes. The superseded claim sitting next to the canonical claim with no distinction is not a minor inconsistency. It is an actively misleading structural record that will produce incorrect downstream design.

**Condition 2: The serial publication constraint.** Published chapters cannot be silently revised. The stability state tracking is not just for your working memory. It is the mechanism that prevents an Unset note from being used as the basis for prose that gets published before the claim is Verified. An explicit Verified state is the gate between design and drafting.

**Condition 3: You are the sole author and the developmental editor simultaneously.** A professional novelist's editor catches the earth pony magic problem during manuscript review. You need a system that catches it during design, because there is no manuscript review phase with an external reader. The four-state model with Superseded as a revision record is the closest available substitute for an editorial revision history.

What would be overengineering: implementing the full architecture across all 108 Stage 0 obligations before doing any further expansion work. The system should be implemented for new content immediately and applied to existing content progressively, starting with the most load-bearing canonical claims that other design work depends on. The earth pony magic entry warrants immediate migration. A note about a minor Tzinacatl cultural detail that has no downstream dependencies can wait.

The correct scope for now is: implement the data model changes (unified Note entity, four states, track structure with Project Notes track), apply immediately to all new content, and migrate existing content in priority order based on what is most likely to be used as a design axiom in the near term.

blocks.rawContent:
## The Precise Taxonomy

Rather than first/second/third order, which implies a linear hierarchy, the correct distinction is by **what the text is made of** and **what it is used for**. These are two independent axes. Let me name each category precisely.

---

### Category 1: Story Content

Text that describes, asserts, or specifies something that exists or occurs within the story's world or the reader's experience of it. It is made of claims about the story. Its use is to be true within the story's frame.

Story Content subdivides into four kinds:

**World truth** — assertions about what is invariantly real in the story's world, independent of any character's knowledge. "Earth pony magic operates through charitostatics and thymodynamics." This is what it is regardless of who knows it or when the reader learns it.

**Historical record** — assertions about what objectively happened, in sequence, causally connected. "The Griffonian Republic was founded in 978. Chrysalis's economic consolidation began with the red love export in 979." Events stated as facts.

**Psychological architecture** — assertions about who a character is and why, independent of what they demonstrate in any given scene. "Twilight's core wound is dependency on external authority for conscience." True regardless of when or whether it is dramatized.

**Thematic proposition** — assertions about what argument the story is making and what evidence must be deposited. "The reader must feel the genuine pull of the counterargument that harmony cannot scale before the confirming evidence arrives." This is story content because it is about what the story does, not about what the author does next.

---

### Category 2: Narrative Architecture

Text that describes how Story Content is structured in time for the reader. It is made of decisions about information flow. Its use is to govern when and how world truths, historical facts, and character psychologies become accessible to the reader and to the POV characters.

Narrative Architecture subdivides into two kinds:

**Macro architecture** — governs information across multiple chapters or the whole story. "The Stagnation's true start date is withheld from characters and reader until Chapter 22. Characters and reader share the 1000-year wrong model together until Celestia's revelation corrects both." This is not a world truth — the world truth is 930 ALB. This is a decision about when that truth enters the reading experience.

**Scene architecture** — governs information within a single scene. "AJ believes she has found her proper place. The reader perceives she has found her hiding place. The FID should render her contentment as genuine. The radio on her back is the non-negotiable physical anchor." This is the experience design for one scene. It is not world truth and not prose.

The reason Narrative Architecture is not Story Content is that it could change without the world being wrong. If you decided to reveal the Stagnation date earlier, the world truth would remain 930 ALB. The architecture would change. These are independent.

The reason Narrative Architecture is not prose is that it specifies what prose must produce without being prose itself. "The reader should feel the contentment as real" is not the sentence that produces that feeling. It is the specification for the sentence.

---

### Category 3: Prose

Text that is the story — language that a reader encounters as the narrative. It is made of words performing voice, sensory experience, rhythm, and FID. Its use is to be read.

Prose subdivides into two kinds:

**Committed prose** — final or near-final language intended to appear in the published work. Lives in the VerbatimText field.

**Prose fragments** — captured phrases, lines, or passages produced during raw capture that may become committed prose. These are currently scattered in Synopsis fields. They are not Scene Architecture — they are linguistic candidates. They belong in a dedicated fragment container, not mixed with delivery sequences.

The reason prose is separate from Narrative Architecture is that the same architecture can be executed by many different prose choices. "Render her contentment as genuine" can be executed by an infinite number of sentences. The architecture is the specification. The prose is one execution of it.

---

### Category 4: Project Management Text

Text that is made of the author's instructions to themselves across time. Its use is to direct future work, record decisions, track obligations, and manage the project's state. It has no story content. It is not readable as part of the story or the story's design. It is correspondence from the author at time T to the author at time T+N.

Project Management Text subdivides into four kinds:

**Obligation** — specifies work that must be done before a piece of content can be treated as Verified. "Research how medieval tally sticks functioned before finalizing Tally Mark's Track B." The obligation is not the content. It is the reason the content is Flagged.

**Revision directive** — records that a canonical claim has changed and specifies what downstream content must be reviewed. "Stagnation start date revised from 0 ALB to 930 ALB. Review: Celestia Track A, all references to 1000-year duration in theme payloads and plot point notes." This is not story content and not architecture. It is a change management record.

**Cross-reference** — records a dependency or connection that is not formally captured in the data model. "This scene's gap depends on the reader having processed the Stalliongrad reports in 12.12. Verify 12.12 is placed correctly in chapter order." This directs future attention without asserting anything about the story.

**Meta-observation** — records the author's current understanding of a design problem without resolving it. "I am not sure whether Mali's backstory should be revealed through her POV or through Fleur's perception. Hold this question." This is not a hypothesis about the world. It is a flag on an unresolved architectural decision.

---

## Why Superseded Should Not Be a Note State

Your instinct is correct. The Superseded state would require a systems engineer reading the World Mechanics track to context-switch into project manager mode to understand why a superseded note is present. The cognitive load is real and the mixing is real.

The correct architecture is: when a canonical claim is revised, the old claim is not retained in the World Mechanics track. It is moved to the **Project Notes track** of the same entity as a Revision Directive. "Prior claim: earth pony magic scales with pride in the crop. Superseded by charitostatic/thymodynamic model after griffonian history expansion. Archived here for reference."

The World Mechanics track then contains only the current canonical claim, Verified. The Project Notes track contains the revision history. A systems engineer reading the World Mechanics track sees only current claims. A project manager reading the Project Notes track sees the revision history. No cognitive mode mixing.

---

## The Flag Field Architecture

Your instinct about the flag and its reason is also correct. Separating the flag from the reason defeats the purpose. When you return to a Flagged note after three weeks, the note says "earth pony magic scales with pride in the crop" and is colored, but the reason for the flag is gone. You have to reconstruct why it was flagged from working memory.

The solution is a **FlagNote** field on the Note entity, separate from the content field. The content field holds Story Content or Narrative Architecture. The FlagNote field holds Project Management Text — specifically the obligation or meta-observation that explains why this note is Flagged.

A note therefore has:

**Content** — the story design assertion. Displayed to a systems engineer.

**FlagNote** — the obligation or reason for flagging. Displayed only when the note is Flagged. Empty when Verified or Unset.

**State** — Unset, Flagged, Verified.

The FlagNote is part of the note entity, not a separate note. It is directly attached to the claim it qualifies. When you read a Flagged claim, you immediately see why it is flagged without navigating to a separate entity.

---

## Visual Separation Within a Track

Yes, they should be visually separated, but by state rather than by arbitrary positioning. The correct visual model is:

**Verified notes** — displayed first, full prominence. These are the canonical truths the track is for. They are what a systems engineer reads.

**Unset notes** — displayed second, reduced prominence. These are candidates. They are visible but marked as provisional.

**Flagged notes** — displayed with a distinct marker and the FlagNote visible. They are neither hidden nor prominent. They signal active work without contaminating the clean read of Verified content.

A reader doing story design reads primarily the Verified notes. A reader doing project management reads the Flagged notes. A reader doing review reads all three in their visual hierarchy. The visual separation enforces the cognitive mode rather than requiring the author to remember to switch modes.

---

## Whether the Second Order Should Split

Yes. The split you identified between Narrative Architecture and Scene Architecture is not a distinction within a single order — it is a distinction between two genuinely different cognitive modes and two different downstream uses.

**World truths, historical record, psychological architecture, and thematic proposition** are Story Content. The cognitive mode for producing them is analytical and systems-oriented. Their downstream use is to be true — to be the axioms against which everything else is calibrated.

**Macro Narrative Architecture** is a decision layer above Story Content. The cognitive mode is strategic and structural — deciding when truth enters the reading experience. Its downstream use is to constrain Scene Architecture.

**Scene Architecture** (POVBelief, ReaderPerception, GapType, FIDAnchors) is a design layer above Macro Architecture. The cognitive mode is rhetorical and psychological — deciding how a specific scene produces a specific experience. Its downstream use is to constrain prose.

**Prose** is the execution layer. The cognitive mode is linguistic and rhythmic.

These are four distinct orders in terms of cognitive mode and dependency. Each depends on the one above it being locally stable. Scene Architecture cannot be correctly designed without Macro Architecture being decided for the relevant information. Macro Architecture cannot be correctly decided without Story Content being canonically established. Prose cannot be correctly drafted without Scene Architecture being specified.

The reason not to call them first/second/third/fourth order is that the word "order" implies they are versions of the same thing at different levels of abstraction. They are not. They are genuinely different kinds of text produced by genuinely different cognitive modes for genuinely different purposes. The names should reflect that difference: Story Content, Macro Architecture, Scene Architecture, Prose.

---

## What Notes to Self Actually Means

From your sampled data, every instance of what functions as a note to self falls into one of the four Project Management Text categories. There is no unified thing called "notes to self." The phrase is an umbrella that covers at least four different things:

From your sample, the Chapter Note "Need to determine the order of Astler, Sickleclaw and Rosewing that makes the best progression and message" is a **Meta-observation** — an unresolved architectural decision flagged for future work.

The note "Fleur has an inkling that Mali worked at a parloir / The letter describes hyper empathy" mixed into a PlotPointCharacter payload is partly a **Psychological architecture claim** about Mali and partly a **Cross-reference** noting that Fleur's perception of Mali is relevant to a future scene.

The note "Need to include an allegory how Celestia did not encourage calculators in school for math" is an **Obligation** — a directive to incorporate a specific element.

The note "Transition to deep third with a sensory hook when emotional stakes rise" from Scene 33.2 is a **Craft observation** — a decision about prose technique that belongs in Scene Architecture or a general craft notes track.

The note appended to a flagged world truth with a question is a **FlagNote** — the reason a canonical claim is not yet Verified.

None of these are the same thing. The phrase "notes to self" conceals this. The correct response is to eliminate the category entirely and replace it with the four Project Management Text types, each going to its correct location: obligations and meta-observations as FlagNotes on the content they qualify, revision directives in the Project Notes track, cross-references in the Project Notes track, craft observations in a Scene Architecture track or general prose notes section.

The fatally general quality of "notes to self" is not a problem with the concept — the problem is that the concept does not exist as a unified thing. It is a label applied to residual text that had no home. Once the homes exist with precise assertion types, the residual disappears because everything has a correct location.

## Prose Examples

### Prose Fragments

Scene 28.3 contains the densest concentration of prose fragments in the sample. These are captured at a quality and specificity that suggests they are intended as close-to-final language:

"I knew what you were, and I loved you anyway."
"I thought I was protecting her. I thought my love was a shield."
