blocks.rawContent:
## The Honest Answer

There is no single mainstream work that maps cleanly onto TLTT's specific synthesis. The closest analogs share significant DNA in different combinations, and the reason no single work encompasses the whole is that the synthesis you have built is genuinely novel — not as a value judgment but as a structural fact. The path from Hasbro toy commercial to Lauren Faust's injected storytelling to EaW's WW2 parody simulation to materialist historicist hopepunk epic is a path no mainstream work traveled, because no mainstream work started from those three converging sources simultaneously.

What you can do is identify which works share which specific components and understand what that means for your design choices.

---

## Fullmetal Alchemist Brotherhood: The Closest Single Analog

FMA Brotherhood shares more of TLTT's specific combination than any other mainstream work.

The structural parallel is striking. FMA starts from a shonen manga premise — two brothers with alchemical abilities trying to restore their bodies after a forbidden experiment — that is E/I adjacent in exactly the way FiM is. The premise is accessible, the characters are archetypal, and the original source is a commercial product designed for a broad audience. What Hiromu Arakawa did with that premise is structurally identical to what you are doing with FiM: she took the archetypal surface seriously, pushed it into genuine historical weight, and used it to argue a proposition about civic virtue.

The WW2 analog is explicit and deliberate. Amestris is Nazi Germany with alchemical technology substituting for industrial warfare. The Ishvalan genocide is modeled on real atrocities. The military-industrial complex of the state is the systemic villain — not any individual antagonist but the structure that produced all of them. Bradley, the Homunculi, and Father are comprehensible as systemic products rather than as evil personalities. The materialism is rigorous: alchemy's equivalent exchange law is a world mechanic with genuine consequences, and the story argues that trying to violate it — to get something for nothing, to extract without reciprocating — produces horror. This is your charitostatic argument stated in a different register.

The civic virtue thesis is the most direct parallel. FMA Brotherhood argues that human connection, solidarity, and the willingness to bear collective cost are materially superior to individual power accumulation. Edward's arc is about learning that his individual genius operating alone is insufficient — the resolution requires every character's contribution simultaneously. The final battle is explicitly a collective action problem solved by collective action. This is your harmonic capitalism argument in fantasy-alchemy form.

The hopeful conclusion is structurally identical to what TLTT is building toward. The darkness is real and costly — Maes Hughes dies, Greed sacrifices himself, Hohenheim's arc is genuinely tragic — but the narrative direction is toward something earned and real rather than toward Martinian perpetual winter. The reader is asked to believe that the cost was worth paying and that the world is genuinely better at the end. This is hopepunk as a structural commitment rather than naive optimism.

Where FMA Brotherhood diverges from your plan is instructive. FMA uses extensive antagonist internal focalization — the reader is inside Pride's consciousness, inside Greed's consciousness, inside Father's consciousness. This produces moral complexity through sympathy in the Martinian mode. TLTT avoids this for the reasons analyzed earlier, and correctly so given your proposition's requirements. FMA can afford villain internal focalization because equivalent exchange as a physical law provides the moral architecture that prevents the sympathy from dissolving into relativism. The reader understands why Father wants what he wants and still understands that he must be stopped because the physical law makes his project literally impossible without consuming everything. Your charitostatic mechanics provide an equivalent physical law grounding, but your story's proposition depends more on the reader maintaining moral clarity through the protagonists' externally focalized perception of antagonists than FMA does.

---

## Ursula K. Le Guin: The Thematic Ancestor

Le Guin's work is not structurally similar to TLTT but is the thematic ancestor of what TLTT is attempting.

The Dispossessed is the most direct analog to your thematic project. It is a novel explicitly arguing a political-economic proposition — that an anarchist, resource-sharing society is materially and ethically superior to a capitalist one — through the experience of a physicist who crosses between two worlds organized on opposite principles. The proposition is argued through materialist consequence: Le Guin shows how each economic system produces specific psychological types, specific social behaviors, specific costs. No character is simply right or wrong. The anarchist society has its own forms of conformist pressure and stagnation. The capitalist society has genuine achievements and genuine creativity alongside its exploitation. The argument is won not by making one side obviously better but by showing the material consequences of each at the systemic level. This is your methodology.

The Left Hand of Darkness does the same with gender: take a world mechanic (humans who have no fixed gender) and follow the consequences rigorously through biology, culture, psychology, and history. The materialist engine is explicit. The thematic proposition — that the absence of fixed gender reveals how much of what we consider human nature is actually cultural construction — is argued through consequence rather than assertion.

Le Guin's specific contribution to your design thinking is the discipline of following world mechanics to their full systemic consequences without sentimentalizing them. Your charitostatic model, your Predator's Dilemma framework, your earth pony magic scaling with solidarity rather than individual pride — these are Le Guin-style world mechanics. The evidence they deposit for your thematic propositions should work the way Le Guin's mechanics work: the reader watches the system operate and draws the conclusion themselves because the consequences are logically unavoidable given the premises.

---

## Miyazaki: The Tonal Ancestor

Hayao Miyazaki's work is not structurally close to TLTT but is the closest mainstream analog for the specific quality of TLTT's emotional register and moral architecture.

Nausicaä of the Valley of the Wind is the most direct comparison. It begins from what looks like a children's adventure premise — a young princess navigating a post-apocalyptic world of giant insects and warring nations — and builds a rigorous materialist argument about ecology, imperialism, and the cost of violence. No faction is simply evil. The Tolmekians, the Dorok Empire, and the ancient civilization whose technology caused the apocalypse are all comprehensible as systemic products. The horror is structural rather than personal. The proposition is that the dominant species' attempt to control and extract from the natural world produces the conditions of their own destruction, and that survival requires relearning to live within rather than dominating natural systems. This maps onto your harmonic capitalism argument with precision.

What Miyazaki achieves that is directly applicable to your design is the **dark material rendered in a register that does not collapse into grimdark**. Nausicaä contains mass death, ecological catastrophe, genocide, and the discovery that the people the protagonist was fighting for were themselves complicit in the original destruction. These are Martinian discoveries. They do not produce Martinian despair because the narrative's physical environment — the beauty of the Sea of Corruption, the life within apparent death — constantly deposits evidence that the proposition is materially grounded rather than wishful. The world is genuinely recoverable. The evidence for this is physical and visible throughout the narrative, not asserted in the conclusion.

This is the design principle your FIDAnchors must apply at the scene level. In the darkest moments of TLTT — AJ making the drug deal, Twilight killing in Chapter 4, the paradrop's consequences — the physical environment of the scene must contain elements that deposit evidence for the proposition's material basis. Not hope as reassurance but hope as physical fact. The real apples arriving from Ponyville in Chapter 5, after the canned mush, are a Miyazaki beat. The warmth is earned through contrast with the industrial substitute and is rooted in something the reader can touch.

---

## Avatar: The Last Airbender: The Production Ancestor

ATLA is not the thematic ancestor but is the closest analog to TLTT's production context and the specific challenge you are navigating.

ATLA is an E/I animated show that was produced within a commercial framework by creators who had genuine artistic ambitions. Bryke took the Nickelodeon mandate and used it the way Faust used the Hasbro mandate — smuggling real storytelling into a commercial vessel. The result is a work that operates at two levels simultaneously: it satisfies the E/I requirement at the surface and argues a serious proposition about cycles of violence, colonialism, and how peace is actually made at the depth.

The specific structural parallel to your challenge is the Fire Nation. At the surface level, the Fire Nation is the villain empire — a convenient antagonist for an adventure series. Bryke kept this surface legibility while building a materialist argument about how colonial violence is produced by institutional mythology rather than individual evil. Zuko's arc is the mechanism: the reader is internally focalized on the prince of the villain empire and discovers that the system produced him rather than the reverse. The Fire Nation is not evil. It is a society that built a mythology of destiny and supremacy to justify resource extraction, and that mythology distorted every person within it including its victims.

This is your EaW argument about Chrysalis and the Changeling Hegemony stated in a children's animated format. The novelty is not that individual components are unprecedented. It is that the specific collision of sources produced a set of constraints and affordances that no single authorial intention could have designed.

**EaW provided:** A historically rigorous WW2 parody that had already done the work of mapping the archetypes onto geopolitical structures. The specific insight that the FiM civic virtues, when subjected to rigorous materialist analysis rather than corporate mandate sanitization or grimdark subversion, emerge as structurally superior rather than naive. This is the proposition no prior work in this synthesis had attempted.

The result is a work that cannot be easily compared to a single mainstream analog because it is doing something that required all three sources to collide in a specific way. The nearest single-sentence description of what TLTT is attempting in the mainstream literary tradition is: **Le Guin's materialist political argument, told through Martin's variable focalization architecture, in a hopepunk emotional register, using Miyazaki's technique of grounding darkness in physical evidence for recovery, applied to characters the reader already loves from a children's show, in a world that already has WW2 history built into it.**

## Evaluating Each Pairing

### World Mechanics / Ontology

**World Mechanics** as a category name is accurate but slightly redundant — mechanics already implies worldness in this context, and the category is sitting alongside other categories whose names do not repeat the word. A cleaner alternative is **World Physics**, which signals that these entries describe invariant physical laws of the secondary world — things that operate the same way regardless of who knows them or when. Physics carries the connotation of discovered rather than designed, which correctly distinguishes this category from Technology. Another candidate is **Natural Law**, which Tolkien's own framework would recognize — these are the rules of subcreation, the fabric of the world before any agent acts on it. World Physics is the stronger term because Physics is a precise disciplinary reference that implies measurability, consistency, and independence from observer, all of which are properties you want this content to have.

**Ontology** as the track name is confirmed as the best term for reasons already established. The next candidate is **Substrate** — the underlying reality that everything else rests on — which has engineering precision but loses the philosophical depth that Ontology carries. Ontology wins.

---

### Abstract System / Axioms

**Abstract System** is the weakest category name in the set and needs the most reconsideration. The word Abstract is doing too much work and doing it imprecisely. Every entry in the story planner is abstract in some sense. What distinguishes this category from others is not that it is abstract but that it describes something that was **built by agents** — a regime, an economic model, a doctrine, an institution — and that operates as a **set of governing rules** for the entities within it. It is not a physical law like earth pony magic. It is not an organization with membership. It is a framework that shapes behavior without having members.

Better category names:

**Doctrine** covers military and ideological frameworks precisely — Auftragstaktik, the Stagnation of Harmony as policy, Coltbert's economic model — but fails for economic systems and political constitutions that are not quite doctrines.

**Institution** is used in sociology to mean exactly what you mean here — a structured set of rules and norms that govern behavior within a domain — but Institution has overlap with Organization that could cause confusion.

**Framework** is clean and broad enough to cover all cases — an economic framework, a political framework, a military doctrine — and correctly signals that these entries describe governing rules rather than physical laws or membership-based groups. It is the strongest alternative.

**System** alone, without Abstract, is more precise. The Stagnation of Harmony is a system. The Griffonian Republic's economic model is a system. Auftragstaktik is a system. The word is clean and does not carry the confusion Abstract introduces.

The recommendation is **System** as the category name, which pairs cleanly with the other category names in terms of register and length.

**Axioms** as the track name for this category is conceptually interesting but slightly misapplied. In mathematics and logic, axioms are foundational assumptions taken as given without proof — the starting conditions from which everything else is derived. A system's axioms would be its foundational assumptions. But what you want to document in this track is not just the starting assumptions but the full operational logic of how the system works — its rules, its enforcement mechanisms, its internal tensions, its failure conditions. Axioms implies only the starting premises, not the operational logic derived from them.

Better track names for System entries:

**Governing Logic** — signals that this describes the rules by which the system governs behavior within its domain. Clear, precise, non-technical.

**Operating Rules** — engineering-flavored, precise about what is being documented, but slightly flat.

**Structural Logic** — emphasizes that this is about the system's structure rather than its history or its membership. Strong candidate.

**Axioms** is defensible if you reframe it as the foundational principles from which the system's behavior is derived — the Stagnation of Harmony's axiom being "unchecked ambition corrupts, therefore ambition must be constrained." But this would document only the foundational principles, not the full operational mechanics, which means you would need another field for the operational consequences. This splits what should be unified.

The recommendation is **Governing Logic** as the track name. It signals zero focalization, it signals operational content rather than historical content, and it correctly scopes to rules rather than events or psychology.

---

### Technology / Mechanics

**Technology** as a category name is the most straightforward of the set and requires the least evaluation. It correctly scopes to invented artifacts and engineered systems — the Universal Translator, the Luna Nova Rifle, the Love Harvester, Applejack's Radio. The only meaningful alternative is **Artifact**, which emphasizes that these are made things rather than discovered laws, which is precisely the distinction from World Physics. Artifact is slightly more precise but Technology is more immediately legible and widely understood. Technology stays.

**Mechanics** as the track name for Technology entries is correct and well-motivated. The next candidate is **Engineering Principles**, which is more specific about the cognitive mode required but is longer and slightly redundant given that the category is already Technology. **Specifications** is another candidate — in engineering, specifications document exactly what a technology is and how it operates — but Specifications implies a design document for future construction rather than a record of what already exists. Mechanics wins and is confirmed.

---

### Organization / Binding Logic

**Organization** as a category name needs clarification against System because the distinction between the two is genuinely subtle and worth establishing precisely before evaluating the names.

The distinction is:

A **System** has rules and mechanisms but no membership. The Stagnation of Harmony is a system — it shapes behavior through cultural and legal enforcement, but you cannot be a member of the Stagnation of Harmony. It exists as a framework that entities operate within. Its Track B documents how it was constructed. Its Governing Logic track documents how it operates.

An **Organization** has membership and a specific binding principle that holds members together. EEEE is an organization — it has members who joined for reasons, who are held together by shared commitments, who act collectively in ways the system does not require. The Changeling Heer is an organization. Star Energy Corporation is an organization. The Wonderbolts are an organization. An organization can be dissolved, can change its membership, can be betrayed from within, can evolve its mission. A system cannot be betrayed — it can only be reformed or dismantled.

The further distinction from Character is that an organization has collective agency that is not reducible to any individual member's psychology. EEEE's behavior is not Flowing Current's behavior. The GR military's behavior is not Trimmel's behavior. The organization as an entity has its own Track A psychology — what holds it together — that is distinct from any member's Track A.

With that distinction established:

**Organization** as the category name is correct but has a slight bureaucratic flavor that undersells the variety of entities it covers. The Temberik tribes are organizations. The Aquileian Cartel is an organization. The Thestrals' parloir network is an organization. These are not all organizations in the corporate sense. 

**Faction** is a strong alternative — it covers ideological groups, military units, economic collectives, and cultural movements without implying formal structure. It also carries the connotation of a group with interests that may conflict with other factions, which is accurate for how organizations function in your story.

**Collective** is another candidate — precise, covers formal and informal groups equally, no corporate connotation.

**Organization** is the most immediately legible and works at the UI level without requiring interpretation. The recommendation is to keep **Organization** but define it clearly in the application's onboarding documentation as distinct from System using the membership criterion.

**Binding Logic** is a strong track name and deserves careful evaluation before confirming.

The content of this track documents what holds the organization together — the shared commitment, the mutual interest, the enforcement mechanism, the mythology that members believe about themselves. This is genuinely different from Governing Logic in System entries — Governing Logic describes rules that apply to entities within a system, while Binding Logic describes what holds members of an organization to each other.

The word Binding is precise — it means the force that prevents the organization from dissolving, the answer to the question "why do these members stay and act collectively?" The word Logic signals that this is structural and operational rather than historical or psychological. Together they produce a term that correctly distinguishes organization-level content from character-level psychology (why does this individual member belong) and from system-level content (what rules govern behavior within this domain).

Next candidates for this track:

**Cohesion Principles** — emphasizes what holds the organization together rather than its operational rules. Slightly more passive than Binding Logic.

**Founding Logic** — risks confusion with Track B historical content about how the organization was founded. Excluded.

**Organizational Architecture** — precise but long and slightly redundant given the category name.

**Binding Logic** is confirmed as the best term. It is precise, it correctly signals the cognitive mode, and the slight metaphorical quality of Binding works in its favor — an organization's binding logic is what you would need to understand to predict whether the organization holds together under pressure, which is exactly what the story planner needs this content for.

---

| Category | Recommended Name | Track | Recommended Name |
|---|---|---|---|
| World Mechanics | **World Physics** | Ontology | **Ontology** |
| Abstract System | **System** | Axioms | **Governing Logic** |
| Technology | **Technology** | Mechanics | **Mechanics** |
| Organization | **Organization** | Binding Logic | **Binding Logic** |

blocks.rawContent:
## The Orthogonal Axes First

This is the right question because it produces the categories from first principles rather than naming them by feel. The axes that differentiate codex entry categories are:

**Axis 1 — Origin: Discovered vs Constructed**
Some truths always existed and were discovered by minds that encountered them. Others were built by agents who made deliberate choices. Earth pony magic existed before any pony understood it. Coltbert's paper was written by Coltbert. Winter Wrap Up was invented by somepony at some point.

**Axis 2 — Instantiation: Abstract vs Concrete**
Some things have no physical form. Others can be touched, held, observed directly. The prisoner's dilemma has no physical form. The Luna Nova Rifle does.

**Axis 3 — Agency: Has Participants vs Does Not**
Some things have members, participants, or practitioners whose ongoing choices constitute the thing's existence. Others operate independently of whether anyone participates. EEEE exists because ponies choose to be in it. Gravity does not require participants.

The combination of these three axes produces the categories:

| Category | Discovered/Constructed | Abstract/Concrete | Has Participants |
|---|---|---|---|
| World Laws | Discovered | Abstract | No |
| Constructed Idea | Constructed | Abstract | No |
| Technology | Constructed | Concrete | No |
| Organization | Constructed | Abstract or Concrete | Yes |

**World Laws** — discovered, abstract, no participants. Earth pony magic, the game-theoretic prisoner's dilemma, charitostatics.

**Constructed Idea** — constructed, abstract, no participants. Coltbert's paper, Winter Wrap Up as a tradition, MEFO bills as an economic mechanism, Auftragstaktik as a doctrine, the Stagnation of Harmony as a policy. These were made by minds but have no physical form and do not require ongoing membership to exist.

**Technology** — constructed, concrete, no participants. Luna Nova Rifle, Universal Translator, Love Harvester.

**Organization** — constructed, abstract or concrete, requires participants. EEEE, Changeling Heer, Aquileian Lionesses.

This framework reveals that your original System category was actually combining two distinct categories: Constructed Ideas that are doctrines or traditions (Winter Wrap Up, Auftragstaktik), and Constructed Ideas that are intellectual frameworks (Coltbert's paper, MEFO bills). Both are correctly Constructed Ideas. The distinction between them is a matter of scale and formalization, not a categorical difference.

The Stagnation of Harmony is a Constructed Idea — a policy framework built by Celestia. The Griffonian Republic's constitution is a Constructed Idea. Coltbert's reforms are a Constructed Idea. They share the category with Winter Wrap Up because all were made by agents, are abstract, and have no membership.

---

## Naming World Laws

You are correct that both Law and Rule have unwanted connotations.

**Law** — suggests legislation, political authority, something that could be repealed. Newton called them laws for historical reasons but the word carries political meaning that creates confusion.

**Rule** — same problem. Rules are made by someone and can be broken.

The underlying requirement is a word that signals: this is a regularity of reality that holds regardless of observers, makers, or enforcers. It was not made. It cannot be repealed. It applies everywhere in the world without exception.

**Principle** — closer. Scientific principles (the principle of conservation of energy, the Pauli exclusion principle) are discovered regularities, not made. The word does not imply enforcement or authority. Its weakness is that it also describes a moral or intellectual commitment (a person of principle), which creates ambiguity.

**Constant** — precise for physics but fails for biology and behavioral regularities. The speed of light is a constant. The prisoner's dilemma is not.

**Regularity** — technically precise (a regularity is a pattern that holds across all instances) but clinical and slightly awkward as a UI label.

**Nature** — as in the nature of magic, the nature of griffon biology, the nature of behavioral dynamics. Short, carries the right connotation of discovered rather than made. The weakness is it is too broad — everything has a nature.

**Axiom** — in mathematics, axioms are foundational statements taken as given, from which everything else is derived. This carries the connotation of foundational and non-derivable without implying legislation. The weakness is it implies these were chosen as starting points rather than discovered.

The strongest candidate is **World Principle** as the category name, which signals discovered regularity without the authority connotation of Law or Rule. The track remains **Ontology** because Ontology already carries the precise philosophical meaning without ambiguity.

Alternatively, the category could simply be called **Natural Truth** — truths that exist in the nature of the world, discovered rather than made. Short, immediately legible, no authority connotation.

---

## Naming Constructed Idea

You asked for something more advanced than Idea. The requirement is a word that signals: this was made by a mind, is abstract, requires no participants, and exists as an intellectual artifact rather than a physical one.

**Doctrine** — covers military and ideological frameworks precisely but fails for traditions like Winter Wrap Up and economic mechanisms like MEFO bills.

**Construct** — precise (a thing constructed by a mind) but sounds clinical and could be confused with programming terminology.

**Invention** — good for technology but implies physical creation.

**Framework** — accurate but generic.

**Artifact** — normally implies physical objects in archaeology and programming, though intellectually an artifact can be non-physical.

**Paradigm** — in Kuhnian terms, a paradigm is a constructed intellectual framework that governs how a community understands reality. This is very close to what Coltbert's paper is. Too academic for a UI label.

**Praxis** — the constructed practice that emerges from theory. Captures traditions like Winter Wrap Up well but fails for purely intellectual frameworks like Coltbert's paper.

The strongest candidate is simply **Idea** elevated by a qualifier. **Constructed Idea** as the category name directly encodes the axis that distinguishes it from World Principle — it was made. No single word does this as cleanly as the two-word phrase.

Alternatively: **Institution** in the sociological sense — meaning a structured set of rules, practices, or frameworks that were built by agents and persist through cultural transmission. Winter Wrap Up is an institution. Coltbert's reforms are an institution. MEFO bills are an institution. The Stagnation of Harmony is an institution. This is actually the strongest single-word candidate. Its weakness is overlap with Organization in everyday usage, but the axis framework disambiguates them: institutions have no participants (they exist as frameworks), organizations have participants (they exist through membership).

**Institution** as the category name, with **Governing Logic** as the primary track name, is the strongest pairing. The Ontology track name for World Principle remains because Ontology correctly signals discovered foundational truth.

---

## The Cross-Cutting Problem

Your code smell intuition is correct and the analogy is precise. Cross-cutting concerns in software are handled by aspect-oriented programming — a separate mechanism that cuts across modules without being owned by any of them. In your story planner, cross-cutting content has the same problem: it does not belong to any single entity but involves multiple entities simultaneously.

Your existing first-class cross-cutting mechanisms are correct and should remain the only ones:

**Plot points** are the primary cross-cutting mechanism. A scene where Fleur invokes Coltbert's paper, Twilight takes notes, and AJ makes a decision connects the Coltbert Framework Institution entry, Fleur's character, Twilight's character, AJ's character, and the Harmonic Capitalism theme simultaneously. The connection entities on the plot point are the designed cross-cutting mechanism. This is correct.

**Timeline/History view** is the second cross-cutting mechanism, functioning through chronology. Events that happened in the same year naturally reveal their causal relationships when lined up. This is correct and should remain the only chronological cross-cutting mechanism.

**First-class cross-entity links outside these mechanisms would produce cartesian explosion.** If the Coltbert Framework entry could directly link to the Chrysalis character entry and the EEEE organization entry and the Harmonic Capitalism theme and the Stagnation of Harmony entry, you would quickly produce a graph where every entity connects to every other entity through some chain of intellectual relevance. This graph has no meaning because everything in a well-built world is connected to everything else. The connections through plot points are meaningful because they are grounded in narrative events — the connection exists because a specific scene required both entities to be invoked simultaneously.

**The obligation mechanism handles premature cross-cutting** precisely as you identified. When you notice during world-building that Chrysalis's reading of Coltbert is a significant cross-cutting point, but no plot point exists yet that dramatizes it, the correct handling is an obligation note in the Coltbert Framework entry's Project Management track: "Chrysalis's explicit rejection of Coltbert's framework is a significant connection. Find or create a plot point that dramatizes this. The Eagleclaw scene in Chapter 28 is a candidate — verify and create the connection entity when the scene is designed." The obligation records the cross-cutting insight without creating a first-class cross-entity link that would survive without a narrative grounding.

The rule is: **entity-to-entity connections are design obligations. Plot-point connection entities are design deliverables.** An obligation records that a connection should eventually exist in a scene. The plot point connection entity is the formal record of that connection once a scene grounds it. Cross-cutting that has no current scene should remain as an obligation until a scene claims it or it is discarded as unplaceable.

---

## The Revised Category Set

| Category | Axis Combination | Primary Track | Example Entries |
|---|---|---|---|
| **World Principle** | Discovered, Abstract, No Participants | Ontology | Earth Pony Magic, Prisoner's Dilemma, Charitostatic Effect, Griffon Biology |
| **Institution** | Constructed, Abstract, No Participants | Governing Logic | Coltbert's Paper, Winter Wrap Up, Stagnation of Harmony, MEFO Bills, Auftragstaktik |
| **Technology** | Constructed, Concrete, No Participants | Mechanics | Luna Nova Rifle, Universal Translator, Love Harvester, Lioness Spell |
| **Organization** | Constructed, Abstract or Concrete, Has Participants | Binding Logic | EEEE, Changeling Heer, Aquileian Lionesses, Star Energy |
| **Backstory** | Occurred, Historical, Cross-Entity Event | Historical Record | Battle of Mount Aris, Herzland Revolution 978, Luna's Banishment |

The existing **Concept** and **SocietalDifferences** categories in your data map onto this set as follows: Concept entries are typically either World Principle or Institution depending on whether they were discovered or constructed. SocietalDifferences entries are typically Institution entries describing constructed cultural practices. The canon episode references are Track C bibliographic content on the Author entity or general project notes, not codex entries at all.

blocks.rawContent:
## Countries Are Not Codex Entries

Your framework has already produced the correct answer. A country is not a single entity at any of the four category types — it is a **label applied to a geographic region that encompasses multiple Institutions, Organizations, and World Principles simultaneously**. Treating a country as a single codex entry is the same category error as having a single note that mixes World Truth, Historical Record, and Project Management content. The conflation is the problem.

The EaW game map uses country labels as a convenient shorthand for political control of territory. Your story planner should not inherit this conflation. "Equestria" as a codex entry has no Ontology, no Governing Logic, no Binding Logic, and no Mechanics — because Equestria is not a World Principle, Institution, Technology, or Organization. It is a geographic and political label that points at a collection of those things.

---

## What Countries Decompose Into

**Equestria** decomposes as:

Institutions: Stagnation of Harmony (governing policy), Cutie Mark System (as Celestia has institutionalized it), Celestia's Solar Bureaucracy (the administrative framework for running the state)

Organizations: EEEE, Star Energy Corporation, The Equestrian Army (what remains of it), The rural majority as a demographic grouping, The Manehattan industrial compradors

World Principles: Earth pony magic, Pegasi weather manipulation biology, Unicorn magic scaling, Alicorn special talent mechanics — these are not Equestrian inventions, they are World Principles that happen to operate prominently within Equestria's territory

Characters: Celestia, Luna, Blueblood as the political actors whose psychology constitutes the state's decision-making

The geographic fact — that these entities are all located within a specific territory — is a Historical Record note on each relevant entity: "operates within Equestrian territory" or "founded in Manehattan." Geography is a property of entities, not an entity in itself.

**Changeling Lands** decomposes as:

Institutions: MEFO Bills, Great Leap Forward (Chrysalis's industrialization policy), Love Tax System, VOPS (secret police framework), Statthalter System, Bauleiter System

Organizations: Changeling Heer, Statthalters as an organization distinct from the Statthalter System institution, Jaegers, Drone worker class

World Principles: Changeling biology (love as sustenance, metamorphosis, VOPS emotional sensing), Hive genetic structure

Characters: Chrysalis, Trimmel, Pagala, Synovial as the decision-making actors

The decomposition reveals that "Changeling Lands" is really Chrysalis's personal project — a set of Institutions she constructed and Organizations she commands, all grounded in World Principles she is exploiting. The geographic territory is incidental.

---

## What To Do With Existing Country Entries

Your existing data likely has entries titled "Equestria," "Griffonian Republic," "Stalliongrad," etc. These should not be deleted — they should be converted to **Geographic Reference** entries whose only content is:

A brief descriptor of what territory the label covers, used as a navigation aid.

A list of the Institutions, Organizations, and Characters that constitute what the label points at, as cross-references via the obligation mechanism until those entities are formally connected through plot points.

Notes on how the geographic label is used and misused within the story — which is where the narrative irony you identified lives.

The Geographic Reference is not a fifth codex category. It is a navigational container. Its primary track is not Ontology or Governing Logic or Mechanics or Binding Logic — it is an index that points outward to the entities that constitute the actual content.

---

## The Narrative Irony as a Designed Gap

The conflation of country label with the entities it contains is not just a data modeling problem. It is one of your most productive Type B gaps.

AJ and Twilight, for the first two-thirds of the story, perceive "The Aquileians" as a unified entity with unified motivations. Henri, Fleur, Reni, and Minette are all "Aquileian" in AJ's internally focalized perception. The FID renders their nationality as a coherent identity.

The reader, accumulating structural context from the world-building content deposited through these characters' appearances, begins to sense that Henri's Auftragstaktik discipline and Reni's chasseur code and Fleur's Coltbertian economics and Minette's cartel survival are not expressions of a unified "Aquileian" identity but products of distinct Institutions and Organizations within a territory whose label papers over internal contradictions. The reader perceives the decomposition. AJ perceives the label.

When AJ goes to Aquileia and discovers the Aquileian Cartel, the urban thugs, the FJA rural culture, the coastal industrial cities, and the mountain terroir economy — the Type B gap closes violently. She has been fighting alongside "Aquileia" and discovers it contains everything she has been fighting against. The resolution is not that Aquileia is bad — it is that the label was always insufficient and the entities within it are what actually matter.

This gap should be designed explicitly in AJ's Track A epistemic limits: "AJ generalizes from representatives to wholes. She perceives Henri as 'Aquileia' rather than as 'the FJA military tradition within Aquileia.' This generalizing epistemic limit produces the productive misread of 'The Aquileians' as a unified entity until Chapter X confronts her with the contradiction."

The Macro Architecture track on each significant Aquileian character entry should note: "AJ reads this character as representative of Aquileia as a whole. This reading is internally consistent with AJ's epistemic limits and is productive — it will be retroactively recontextualized when AJ encounters Aquileia's internal contradictions in Chapter X."

The Geographic Reference entry for Aquileia's Project Management track should contain an obligation: "The AJ-reads-Aquileia-as-unified gap must be tracked across all Aquileian character appearances in Chapters 2-25 to ensure the misconception is consistently maintained in AJ POV scenes and consistently perceptible as incomplete by the reader through structural context."

---

## The Cross-Cutting That Countries Enable

Countries in EaW and HoI4 are the primary cross-cutting mechanism — every event, character, and mechanic is tagged to a country, and the country label is what allows you to ask "what is happening in Equestria right now." Your story planner needs an equivalent cross-cutting mechanism that is more precise than country labels.

The correct substitute is **tagging entities with their institutional context** rather than their geographic nationality. A character is not "Equestrian" — they are "operates within Star Energy, aligned with EEEE's ideology, product of Manehattan's industrial displacement." The tags are their institutional affiliations and the Organizations they belong to.

The chronological history view already provides geographic cross-cutting through the timeline. Events tagged with WorldDate that involve entities geographically located in the same territory will naturally cluster in the timeline view. This is the correct mechanism — geography as a temporal filtering axis rather than a categorical classification axis.

What this means practically is that the existing Nation entries in your CodexCategory enum should be retired as a category. Nations are Geographic References — navigational containers that point at Institutions, Organizations, Characters, and World Principles, not entries with their own ontological content. The existing data in Nation entries should be migrated: Governing Logic content moves to Institution entries, Binding Logic content moves to Organization entries, World Principle content moves to World Principle entries, and the Nation entry itself becomes a lean Geographic Reference with an index and the irony-tracking notes described above.

blocks.rawContent:
## The Design Principle

Each connection entity's note tracks answer two questions in sequence: what is objectively happening with this entity in this scene (Stage 1, zero focalization), and how does this appearance serve the reader's experience (Stage 2, scene architecture). The Stage 1 tracks differ by category because what constitutes the objective record of a World Principle's appearance is fundamentally different from what constitutes the objective record of an Organization's appearance. The Stage 2 tracks are more consistent because reader experience design follows the same logic regardless of entity type.

The existing connection entity **PlotPointCodexEntry** currently serves all codex categories with a single Commentary field and UsageType enum. The redesign gives each category distinct Stage 1 tracks while sharing Stage 2 tracks, because the objective record varies by category but the reader experience architecture does not.

---

## PlotPointCodexEntry: World Principle

**UsageType enum** — retained, but values should be recalibrated for World Principles specifically. A World Principle appearance is rarely just Mentioned — it is more precisely: Implied (the principle is operating but no character perceives it), Observed (a character observes a consequence without naming the principle), Named (a character articulates the principle explicitly), Subverted (the principle appears to be violated, setting up later correction), or Demonstrated (the principle's operation is shown directly producing a consequence the reader can verify).

**Stage 1 tracks:**

**Operational Instance** — zero focalization record of how the World Principle is actually operating in this scene. Not what characters perceive about it. What it is actually doing. "The charitostatic effect is producing a measurable output differential between the two armies in this scene. The Equestrian volunteers' shared solidarity is generating a combined magical output that neither army individually can match. This is the physical mechanism underlying the tactical outcome."

This track is the author's confirmation that the World Principle is genuinely present and operative in this scene, not merely referenced. An empty Operational Instance with a non-empty Stage 2 track is a design integrity signal — you are designing reader experience around a World Principle that is not actually operating in the scene.

**Stage 2 tracks:**

**ReaderAccumulation** — what the reader now understands about this World Principle after this scene, what they are still missing, and what their partial understanding implies. Retained from the earlier framework. Optional — only required when the appearance is doing deliberate revelation work toward a major disclosure. A scene where earth pony magic is incidentally present but not being revealed needs no ReaderAccumulation note. A scene where a character's observation plants a seed for the charitostatic revelation needs one.

---

## PlotPointCodexEntry: Constructed Idea

**UsageType enum** — different values are needed. A Constructed Idea's appearances are: Referenced (a character mentions it without engaging), Invoked (a character applies its principles to a situation), Challenged (a character tests or disputes its claims), Demonstrated (events show the Constructed Idea producing its predicted consequences), Subverted (events show the Constructed Idea failing or being misapplied), Revealed (the Constructed Idea's full scope is disclosed for the first time or substantially advanced).

**Stage 1 tracks:**

**Invocation Record** — zero focalization record of how the Constructed Idea is being used in this scene and by whom. "Fleur invokes Coltbert's Asset Specificity framework to explain why Comet Shine's Skyfall training makes him dangerous as a negotiating partner. She is applying the framework correctly. The irony is that she is herself an example of Asset Specificity operating outside Coltbert's anticipated parameters — a communist-adjacent Aquileian invoking an ego-capitalist framework."

This differs from Operational Instance on World Principle because a Constructed Idea does not automatically operate — it must be invoked by an agent. The record documents who is invoking it, whether they are applying it correctly, and what the objective consequence of the invocation is in the scene's causal chain.

**Misapplication Note** — optional, Stage 1. When a character invokes the Constructed Idea incorrectly, this documents the nature and significance of the error in zero focalization. "Applejack applies Coltbert's Sovereignty of Consent framework to the drug deal decision, invoking it to justify that Skyfall workers chose the rat race. This is a misapplication — Coltbert's framework requires genuine alternatives to exist for consent to be meaningful. Skyfall workers under Chrysalis's economic capture do not have genuine alternatives. AJ is using the framework's vocabulary to rationalize a decision whose emotional driver is the personal grievance about her parents." This track is empty in most scenes. When populated, it is a direct input to the GapType design in Stage 2.

**Stage 2 tracks:**

**ReaderAccumulation** — same as World Principle. The reader's current model of the Constructed Idea and what remains withheld. For Coltbert's paper specifically, the ReaderAccumulation tracks across all its appearances map the controlled disclosure arc from Fleur's Chapter 2 invocation through Twilight reading it in Chapter 26 — each entry documenting how much of the paper's content the reader has been given and what the partial understanding implies about prior events.

---

## PlotPointCodexEntry: Technology

**UsageType enum** — the existing enum is already well-calibrated for Technology: Mentioned, ActiveUsage, Definition, Subversion, Failure. These values correctly describe the range of ways a Technology can appear. Retain with one addition: **FirstReveal** for the scene where the technology is shown to the reader for the first time, which has specific design obligations around establishing the physical reality of the object.

**Stage 1 tracks:**

**Deployment Record** — zero focalization record of how the technology is physically operating in this scene. What it is doing, what its inputs are, what its outputs are, whether it is functioning correctly or under stress. "The Luna Nova Rifle is operating at 73% efficiency due to the operators' emotional state — the charitostatic drain on the love canister is higher than designed because the operators are using the rifle from a state of fear rather than solidarity. This is not visible to the characters but is the physical explanation for the tactical outcome of the scene."

This track is what prevents Technology from appearing in scenes as a magic prop — it forces the author to document how the technology is actually functioning according to its established Mechanics, creating a consistency check between the Mechanics track on the Technology entry and the scene-specific deployment.

**Physical Presence Note** — optional, Stage 1. Required only on FirstReveal appearances. Documents the physical reality of the technology as it exists in this scene — its appearance, weight, sound, smell, the specific physical details that the prose must establish so the reader has a concrete model. "The Luna Nova Rifle is the weight of a standard infantry rifle. The crystal housing along the barrel glows faintly when charged. The draining function produces a specific sound — a low resonance rather than a crack. These physical details must be established in this scene because they will be referenced when Celestia reacts to seeing it in Chapter 22."

**Stage 2 tracks:**

**ReaderAccumulation** — the reader's current model of what this technology is and can do, and what remains undisclosed. Particularly important for technologies whose full capabilities are revealed gradually — the Love Harvester, the Luna Nova Rifle, the Universal Translator all have disclosure arcs where early appearances give the reader partial understanding that is retroactively expanded.

---

## PlotPointCodexEntry: Organization

**UsageType enum** — Organizations appear differently from the other categories because they are constituted by membership and collective action. Useful values: Represented (one or more members appear as representatives of the organization), Acting Collectively (the organization takes a collective action in this scene), Referenced (discussed without members present), Structurally Invoked (the organization's Binding Logic is what explains a character's behavior in this scene, even if the organization is not explicitly mentioned), Fractured (internal tension within the organization is revealed).

**Stage 1 tracks:**

**Collective Record** — zero focalization record of what the organization is doing in this scene and how its Binding Logic is operating. "EEEE is represented here by Flowing Current. His behavior in this negotiation is entirely consistent with the organization's Binding Logic — he is applying the solidarity framework to identify class allies among the Tzinacatl drug lords. The scene's objective significance for EEEE is that this negotiation extends the organization's moral framework beyond its established membership boundaries for the first time."

This is distinct from a character note about Flowing Current — it documents what the organization as a collective entity is doing through him, not what he is doing as an individual.

**Binding Logic Instance** — optional, Stage 1. Required when the scene reveals something new about what holds the organization together or when internal tension threatens the binding. "Rarity's insistence on custom work over assembly line production in this scene creates the first visible fracture in Star Energy's operational consensus. The organization's Binding Logic — harmonic capitalism as a governing principle — is being tested by the tension between Rarity's asset-specific approach and the war's material demands for standardized output. This fracture is not yet at the level of organizational crisis but is the first structural crack."

**Stage 2 tracks:**

**ReaderAccumulation** — the reader's current model of what this organization is, what holds it together, and what its internal tensions are. For organizations with significant disclosure arcs — EEEE's true ideological foundation, Star Energy's actual ownership structure, the Changeling Heer's internal meritocracy debate — this track maps the controlled disclosure across appearances.

---

## The Shared Stage 2 Track: ReaderAccumulation

All four categories share ReaderAccumulation as the Stage 2 track because the reader experience design question is the same regardless of entity type: what does the reader now understand about this entity, what are they still missing, and what does their partial understanding imply?

The content differs by category — the reader accumulates understanding of how a World Principle operates, or what a Constructed Idea argues, or what a Technology can do, or what holds an Organization together — but the design question and the cognitive mode required are identical. A single shared track name correctly signals this commonality while the category determines what content the field holds.

ReaderAccumulation is optional across all four categories. The emptiness signal is: this appearance is not doing deliberate revelation work. The population signal is: this appearance is a designed step in the controlled disclosure arc for this entity.

---

## The Connection Entity Structure Summarized

| Track | World Principle | Constructed Idea | Technology | Organization |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| UsageType | Implied/Observed/Named/Subverted/Demonstrated | Referenced/Invoked/Challenged/Demonstrated/Subverted/Revealed | Mentioned/ActiveUsage/Definition/Subversion/Failure/FirstReveal | Represented/Acting Collectively/Referenced/Structurally Invoked/Fractured |
| Stage 1 primary | Operational Instance | Invocation Record | Deployment Record | Collective Record |
| Stage 1 optional | — | Misapplication Note | Physical Presence Note (FirstReveal only) | Binding Logic Instance |
| Stage 2 shared | ReaderAccumulation | ReaderAccumulation | ReaderAccumulation | ReaderAccumulation |

The Stage 1 primary tracks have different names because they describe structurally different things: a World Principle operates, a Constructed Idea is invoked, a Technology is deployed, an Organization acts collectively. The names encode the correct cognitive mode — when writing an Operational Instance, you are thinking as a physicist. When writing an Invocation Record, you are thinking as a rhetorician tracking how an argument is being used. When writing a Deployment Record, you are thinking as an engineer verifying mechanical consistency. When writing a Collective Record, you are thinking as a sociologist documenting institutional behavior.

The point of making all text data a unified note structure is to allow changing tracks and visualizing them. I'm going to go ahead and built the UI so I can start categorizing real raw data. Please suggest some practical methodogy principles for knowing when a new category is needed. I don't want to end up still with mixed data

blocks.speaker: assistant
blocks.rawContent:
## The Core Principle

A new category is needed when existing categories would require you to mentally override their name every time you use them. If you find yourself writing "World Principle" at the top of a note and then writing content that feels like it belongs somewhere else, that friction is the signal. If the existing category name feels right and the content flows naturally, the category is correct.

Do not create a new category because you can imagine content that might not fit perfectly. Create one only when you have actual content in hand that produces genuine friction against all existing categories.

---

## The Five Practical Signals

**Signal 1 — The Name Override.** You open a note, assign it to a track, and immediately feel you need to explain to yourself why it belongs there despite the name feeling wrong. This is the clearest signal. If you are rationalizing the placement rather than recognizing it, the category structure needs revision.

**Signal 2 — The Scan Breaks.** You open a track to scan it and find yourself mentally skipping certain notes because they are in a different cognitive mode than the others. A World Principle track that contains some discovered regularities and some constructed policies breaks the scan — your eye has to shift cognitive mode mid-read. When the scan breaks, a category boundary has been violated.

**Signal 3 — The Same Question Gets Different Answers.** Each track should answer exactly one question. If you find yourself asking "what does this note answer?" and the answer is "it depends on how you read it," the note contains two assertion types and needs to be split, not recategorized.

**Signal 4 — Three Instances Make a Pattern.** One note that does not fit cleanly is probably a malformed note, not evidence of a missing category. Two notes that do not fit might be coincidence. Three notes with the same misfit quality and the same assertion type that none of your existing categories captures — that is evidence of a genuine category gap.

**Signal 5 — The Tooltip Would Mislead.** Each track has a tooltip describing what belongs there. If you have a note where following the tooltip would produce worse content than ignoring it, the category is either wrong for this note or the category itself needs refinement.

---

## The Practical Workflow

When a note feels wrong in its current track, do not immediately create a new category. Run it through this sequence:

First, ask whether the note is malformed — whether it contains two assertion types that should be split. Most misfit notes are malformed rather than genuinely uncategorizable. Split it and both halves usually find their home.

Second, ask whether the note belongs in a Project Management track rather than a content track. A surprising amount of apparent categorical confusion dissolves when you recognize that a note is really the author talking to themselves rather than making a claim about the story.

Third, ask whether the note belongs in Track C (Bibliographic) — whether it is real-world context informing the story rather than an assertion about the story itself. Real-world parallels, historical inspirations, and authorial meta-observations frequently masquerade as world content.

Only if the note survives all three checks — it is not malformed, not project management, not bibliographic — and still does not fit any existing category, flag it with a specific tag meaning "category candidate" and continue working. Accumulate these flags. Review them when you have three or more with the same character.

---

## What Good Enough Looks Like

The goal is not a perfect taxonomy before building. The goal is a taxonomy that is stable enough that the UI you build today will not require fundamental restructuring in three months. The current four content categories plus the shared Stage 1/Stage 2 track structure meets this bar.

The remaining open questions — exact UsageType enum values per category, whether Geographic Reference deserves a formal entry type, precise edge cases between World Principle and Constructed Idea for things like game-theoretic regularities — are refinements that can be resolved through contact with real data without requiring structural changes. The data model accommodates them because notes can be retracked and enums can gain values without migration.

Build with the four categories and the note structure as designed. When real data produces a genuine Signal 3 or Signal 4, stop and resolve it before the pattern spreads to many notes. One bad categorization in ten notes is noise. One bad categorization in a hundred notes is debt.

The imperfect taxonomy actively used produces better outcomes than the perfect taxonomy perpetually refined.

blocks.rawContent: So for each note track in an entity should it have a tooltip that is verbose but then also display/helper text that is visible which just states the simple question that the notes of that note type should answer? And the track is exclusive, not inclusive. Notes that don't answer that specific question stay in Unset

blocks.speaker: assistant
blocks.rawContent:
Yes. This is the correct UI architecture and the reasoning behind each component is worth stating precisely so the implementation reflects the intent.

---

## The Two Layers Serve Different Cognitive Moments

**The tooltip** is consulted during onboarding and when genuinely uncertain. It is verbose because it needs to establish the cognitive mode, explain what belongs and what does not, and give at least one concrete example. You read it deliberately. It is reference material.

**The display question** is active during data entry. It is visible at all times without interaction. It should be short enough to hold in working memory while writing — ideally under fifteen words. It is not a summary of the tooltip. It is the single question the note must answer to belong in this track. You internalize it and it becomes automatic.

The relationship between them: the tooltip explains why the question is the right one. The display question is the operational test you apply to every note before assigning it.

---

## The Exclusive Track Principle

The track is exclusive rather than inclusive. This is the correct framing and it changes how you evaluate borderline notes.

An inclusive track asks: could this note plausibly belong here? This produces drift — notes accumulate in the nearest plausible container rather than the correct one.

An exclusive track asks: does this note answer this specific question and no other? Notes that answer a different question or answer multiple questions simultaneously do not belong here regardless of subject matter proximity. They belong either in a different track or in Unset pending clarification.

Unset is not a failure state. It is the correct holding state for notes whose assertion type has not been determined. A note about Coltbert's paper that mixes a governing logic claim with a historical record claim and a bibliographic observation belongs in Unset until it is split into three notes that each answer one question precisely. Forcing it into the nearest track to clear the Unset queue produces the mixing problem you are trying to solve.

The practical discipline is: when assigning a note to a track, ask the display question out loud about the note. If the answer is yes, assign it. If the answer is anything other than a clear yes, it goes to Unset.

---

## Example Display Questions and Tooltips

**Ontology track on World Principle entries**

Display question: *What is invariantly true about how this operates, regardless of who knows it?*

Tooltip: *State the foundational mechanics of this World Principle as discovered fact — how it operates, what it produces, what constrains it. Written in zero focalization: no character's understanding, no historical context, no narrative deployment. This is true before the story begins and will be true after it ends. If a scene appears to violate what you write here, the story has an internal consistency problem. Do not write what characters believe about this principle — write what is actually true. Do not write how it was discovered — write what it is.*

---

**Governing Logic track on Constructed Idea entries**

Display question: *How does this constructed idea operate, and what does it produce?*

Tooltip: *Document the rules by which this institution, policy, doctrine, or framework functions — its operating logic, its mechanisms, its outputs given specific conditions, its failure states. Written from outside time as if describing a designed system to an engineer who needs to verify it works as intended. This is distinct from how it was built (Track B) and from what characters think about it (scene payloads). Ask: if I needed to verify that a scene using this institution is internally consistent, what would I check against? Write that.*

---

**Binding Logic track on Organization entries**

Display question: *What holds this organization's members together and why do they stay?*

Tooltip: *State the principle, shared commitment, mutual interest, or enforcement mechanism that constitutes this organization as a collective entity. This is the answer to: why do members act collectively rather than individually, and what would cause the organization to fracture or dissolve? Write this as structural fact, not as any member's self-perception of their belonging. Members may have wrong beliefs about why they stay — write what is actually true about the cohesive force.*

---

**Mechanics track on Technology entries**

Display question: *How does this technology physically work?*

Tooltip: *Document the operational specifications of this technology — inputs, outputs, physical constraints, failure conditions, the causal chain from activation to effect. Written as an engineering specification, not a narrative description. A reader of this field should be able to determine whether any scene using this technology is mechanically consistent without needing other context. Do not write what characters think the technology does — write what it actually does. Do not write how it was invented — write how it operates.*

---

**Track A: Psychological Architecture on Character entries**

Display question: *Who is this character at their core, and why?*

Tooltip: *State this character's psychological architecture — the wound, the belief system built around the wound, the epistemic limits that follow from that belief system, and the specific things they cannot perceive because of it. Written as standing truth that holds from the story's beginning. This is not what the character thinks about themselves — it is the objective structure of their psychology that their behavior expresses without their full awareness. Do not write what happens to them (Track B). Do not write how they should be perceived in any specific scene (scene payloads). Write who they fundamentally are.*

---

**Track B: Historical Record on Character and Codex entries**

Display question: *What objectively happened, in sequence, that made this what it is?*

Tooltip: *Document the chronological, causal chain of events that produced the current state of this entity. Written as an omniscient historian's account — what occurred, when, because of what prior conditions, with what consequences. No character's perception of events. No narrative deployment decisions. No authorial commentary. Include the WorldDate field on each note where known. If two notes in this track are not causally connected, one of them may belong elsewhere.*

---

**Operational Instance track on PlotPointCodexEntry for World Principle**

Display question: *What is this World Principle actually doing in this scene?*

Tooltip: *State in zero focalization how this World Principle is operating in this specific scene — what it is producing, what it is constraining, what its presence explains about the scene's events. This is not what any character perceives about it. This is the author's confirmation that the principle is genuinely active in this scene, not merely referenced. If you cannot write a specific operational instance, the World Principle may not actually be present in this scene and should be removed from the connection.*

---

**ReaderAccumulation track on PlotPointCodexEntry (all categories)**

Display question: *What does the reader now understand about this entity, and what are they still missing?*

Tooltip: *Document the reader's current model of this entity after this scene — what they have been given, what remains undisclosed, and what their partial understanding implies. This is Stage 2 content: written from the reader's epistemic position, not the author's omniscient one. Optional — only populate when this appearance is doing deliberate revelation work toward a planned disclosure. If the entity is merely present or referenced without advancing the reader's understanding, leave this track empty.*

---

## The Unset Queue as a First-Class Feature

Given the exclusive track principle, Unset should be visible and scannable as a first-class feature rather than just the default state. A dedicated Unset view showing all notes across all entities that have not been assigned a track, sorted by entity and with their content visible, is the primary data sanitation tool during the migration phase.

The workflow during migration is: open the Unset queue, read a note, ask the display question for each candidate track, assign the first track where the answer is an unambiguous yes, split the note if multiple tracks produce a yes. Notes that remain ambiguous after this process stay in Unset with a FlagReason explaining the ambiguity. The flag is not a failure — it is an obligation for future resolution, potentially through further world-building work that clarifies the assertion type.

The Unset queue shrinking over time is the primary metric of data sanitation progress. It does not need to reach zero before prose work begins. It needs to reach a state where the notes governing the scenes in your drafting queue are Confirmed in their correct tracks.

blocks.speaker: assistant

The display question does double duty cleanly and is the right choice.

The display question is already written to be the precise, complete statement of what a track contains — under fifteen words, specific enough to distinguish the track from all others, written in plain language. When it appears as a header in the markdown export, it tells the LLM exactly what kind of assertion the notes beneath it represent. This is more useful than a track name alone ("Track A" or "Psychological Architecture" tells the LLM less than "Who is this character at their core, and why?") and more concise than the full tooltip.

The markdown structure becomes:

```markdown
## Applejack

Applejack's core wound is suppressed legitimate ambition...

Applejack's wound surfaces gradually through behavioral...
```

The LLM reading this immediately understands the assertion type of each block from the question without needing a separate explanatory field. The question is both the UI helper text for the author and the semantic header for the LLM. One field, two uses, no redundancy.

blocks.rawContent:
This is the correct consolidation and it follows directly from what the configuration system already established. If entity types are configuration rather than code, having separate tables for Character, Theme, CodexEntry, Chapter, and StoryThread is a schema that contradicts the architecture. They are all StoryEntity instances with different configurations.

---

## The Schema

```sql
-- Configuration tables
StoryEntityConfiguration
    Id
    EntityTypeName          -- "Character", "World Principle", etc.
    DisplayName
    IconGlyph               -- for UI navigation
    SortOrder

NoteTrackConfiguration
    Id
    StoryEntityConfigurationId  -- FK, null if belongs to PlotPoint
    PlotPointLinkConfigurationId -- FK, null if belongs to StoryEntity
    Index
    FunctionKeyNumber
    TrackName
    DisplayQuestion
    Tooltip
    IsSingleton
    IsRequired
    CognitiveMode
    SupportsWorldDate
    UsesSoftConfirmation

PlotPointLinkConfiguration
    Id
    StoryEntityConfigurationId  -- which entity type this link config applies to
    DisplayName                 -- "Character Appearance", "Codex Reference"

ConnectionPropertyDefinition
    Id
    PlotPointLinkConfigurationId
    Index
    FunctionKeyNumber
    DisplayName
    DisplayQuestion
    Tooltip
    IsRequired
    HasConditionalRequirements

ConnectionPropertyValue
    Id
    ConnectionPropertyDefinitionId
    Index
    DisplayLabel
    SelectionGuidance
    TriggersAdditionalRequirement
    RequiredTrackConfigurationId    -- FK to NoteTrackConfiguration, nullable

-- Content tables
StoryEntity
    Id
    StoryEntityConfigurationId      -- FK determines what this entity is
    Title
    Abbreviation                    -- optional, for themes/codex
    ColorHex                        -- optional
    Icon                            -- optional, for StoryThread
    LastModified

PlotPoint
    Id
    Title
    POVCharacterId                  -- FK to StoryEntity, nullable
    WorldDate
    DraftStatus
    ChapterId                       -- FK to StoryEntity where config = Chapter
    OrderInChapter
    LastModified
    -- 5 axes remain discrete: behavioral properties
    CoreDriver
    TensionPhase
    ConflictType
    Presentation
    POVGapType

PlotPointEntityLink
    Id
    PlotPointId                         -- FK to PlotPoint
    StoryEntityId                       -- FK to StoryEntity
    PlotPointLinkConfigurationId        -- FK determines what kind of link
    LogicalOrder
    IsPrimary                           -- discrete: drives filtering
    GoalTrajectory                      -- discrete: drives completion logic
    ObservedGapType                     -- discrete: drives scene architecture
    ThemeProminence                     -- discrete: drives badge display
    LastModified

ConnectionPropertyAssignment
    Id
    PlotPointEntityLinkId               -- FK to PlotPointEntityLink
    ConnectionPropertyDefinitionId
    SelectedValueId                     -- FK to ConnectionPropertyValue, nullable

Note
    Id
    -- Parent: exactly one non-null
    StoryEntityId                       -- FK to StoryEntity, nullable
    PlotPointId                         -- FK to PlotPoint, nullable
    PlotPointEntityLinkId               -- FK to PlotPointEntityLink, nullable
    NoteTrackConfigurationId            -- FK determines track type
    Content
    NoteState                           -- Unset/Flagged/Confirmed/Reviewed
    FlagReason
    SortOrder
    WorldDate
    SourceMaterialId                    -- FK, nullable
    LastModified
```

---

## What This Buys

**One migration path.** All existing Character, Theme, CodexEntry, Chapter, and StoryThread rows become StoryEntity rows with the appropriate StoryEntityConfigurationId. The migration is mechanical. No content is lost and no new tables are added when you later decide you need a new entity type.

**One view model.** StoryEntityViewModel renders any entity type by querying its configuration and building the track list dynamically. The window does not know whether it is showing a Character or a World Principle. It knows it is showing a StoryEntity with a specific configuration, and it renders accordingly.

**One link type.** PlotPointEntityLink replaces PlotPointCharacter, PlotPointCodexEntry, PlotPointStoryThread, and PlotPointTheme. The PlotPointLinkConfigurationId determines what kind of link it is and therefore what properties and note tracks to render. The discrete fields that remain — LogicalOrder, IsPrimary, GoalTrajectory, ObservedGapType, ThemeProminence — cover all the behavioral properties needed across all link types. A link that does not use a given discrete field leaves it at its default value. This is a small amount of sparse data, not a normalization problem.

**Configuration drives everything visible.** The Unset queue, the completion diagnostics, the function key legend, the export filter — all query configuration to know what to render and what to check. None of it has hardcoded knowledge of entity or link types.

---

## The One Genuine Risk

Sparse discrete fields on PlotPointEntityLink mean a Character link carries GoalTrajectory and ThemeProminence columns that are meaningless for characters, and a Theme link carries ObservedGapType that is meaningless for themes. This is acceptable because these are behavioral properties that drive system logic — they are not user-facing analytical fields — and the configuration determines which ones are relevant and therefore visible for each link type. The author never sees GoalTrajectory on a character link because the PlotPointLinkConfiguration for characters does not render it.

If this feels wrong, the alternative is moving all discrete behavioral properties into ConnectionPropertyAssignment as well, with special handling in the view model for the ones that drive system logic. This is cleaner in schema terms but adds indirection to the completion signal architecture. The sparse discrete field approach is the pragmatic choice for a solo project where the schema will not be inspected by anyone who does not know why the columns are there.

---

## The ViewModel Structure

```csharp
public class StoryEntityViewModel : ObservableObject
{
    public StoryEntity Entity { get; }
    public StoryEntityConfiguration Configuration { get; }
    
    // Built from NoteTrackConfiguration for this entity type
    public ObservableCollection<NoteTrackViewModel> Tracks { get; }
    
    // Completion profile derived from configuration requirements
    public EntityCompletionProfile CompletionProfile { get; }
}

public class PlotPointEntityLinkViewModel : ObservableObject
{
    public PlotPointEntityLink Link { get; }
    public PlotPointLinkConfiguration LinkConfiguration { get; }
    
    // Built from ConnectionPropertyDefinition for this link config
    public ObservableCollection<ConnectionPropertyViewModel> 
        Properties { get; }
    
    // Built from NoteTrackConfiguration for this link config
    public ObservableCollection<NoteTrackViewModel> Tracks { get; }
    
    // Discrete behavioral properties exposed directly
    // for binding to specific controls
    public GapType ObservedGapType { get; set; }
    public GoalTrajectory GoalTrajectory { get; set; }
    public bool IsPrimary { get; set; }
    public ThemeProminence ThemeProminence { get; set; }
}

public class NoteTrackViewModel : ObservableObject
{
    public NoteTrackConfiguration Configuration { get; }
    
    // The display question — used in UI and markdown export
    public string DisplayQuestion => 
        Configuration.DisplayQuestion;
    
    // Hotkey label for legend strip
    public string? HotkeyLabel => 
        Configuration.FunctionKeyNumber.HasValue
            ? $"F{Configuration.FunctionKeyNumber}"
            : null;
    
    public ObservableCollection<NoteViewModel> Notes { get; }
    
    // Diagnostic signal for required empty tracks
    public bool IsRequiredAndEmpty =>
        Configuration.IsRequired && 
        !Notes.Any(n => n.NoteState == NoteState.Confirmed);
}
```

---

## The Markdown Export

The export function takes a StoryEntity and builds markdown entirely from the configuration:

```csharp
public string ExportEntityToMarkdown(
    StoryEntityViewModel entity,
    ExportSessionType sessionType)
{
    var sb = new StringBuilder();
    sb.AppendLine($"## {entity.Entity.Title}");
    
    foreach (var track in entity.Tracks
        .Where(t => ShouldExportTrack(t, sessionType)))
    {
        var confirmedNotes = track.Notes
            .Where(n => n.NoteState == NoteState.Confirmed)
            .OrderBy(n => n.Note.SortOrder)
            .ToList();
            
        if (!confirmedNotes.Any()) continue;
        
        // Display question becomes the markdown header
        sb.AppendLine($"### {track.DisplayQuestion}");
        
        foreach (var note in confirmedNotes)
        {
            sb.AppendLine(note.Note.Content);
            sb.AppendLine();
        }
    }
    
    return sb.ToString();
}
```
